stories.title: Slogans raised in Lucknow demanding UGC rollback:LU students took to streets; warn of rising caste tensions on campus
stories.summary: Protests against the new rules of the University Grants Commission (UGC) have intensified in Lucknow. Students from many colleges, including Lucknow University, have taken to the streets. Strong demonstrations are ongoing outside the LU campus. Students are raising slogans against the UGC Act of 2026. They are demanding a UGC rollback. Students say this is UGC's black law. Until the government withdraws it, we will not back down. Student Arpit Tiwari said - Through UGC, there is an attempt to victimize SC/ST students. This is an attempt to directly declare general category students as criminals. Student Akarsh Mishra said - UGC's new rules will increase caste conflict on campus. He concluded his statement with the poetic lines - 'The battle is not over, the hunter is not the only bearer of sin, those who remain neutral, time will record their crimes too.' In view of the violent protests by students, a heavy police force has been deployed on campus by the LU administration. All gates including LU's main gate Bhaurao Deoras Gate have been closed. Student entry has been banned on campus for some time. The proctor and administrative officers are present at the scene. Why oppose UGC's new rules? UGC notified its new rules on January 13. It is called - 'Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions Regulations, 2026.' Under this, instructions have been given to form special committees, helplines, and monitoring teams to prevent caste-based discrimination in colleges and universities. These teams will specifically look into complaints from SC, ST, and OBC students. The government says these changes have been made to bring fairness and accountability in higher education institutions. However, the rules are being opposed by calling them against the general category. Critics say that upper-caste students have been made 'natural criminals'. General category students say that the new rules could promote discrimination against them on college or university campuses. This will create chaos in colleges.

stories.title: Ayodhya GST Deputy Commissioner resigns in support of CM Yogi:Prashant Singh says, 'Won't tolerate CM's insult, Shankaracharya’s comments crossed the line'
stories.summary: The controversy of Shankaracharya in UP is now growing. Now, Ayodhya's GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar Singh has resigned in support of PM Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and CM Yogi. He said that he felt very bad about Shankaracharya's comments on the CM. I am hurt by this. I can no longer tolerate the insult of the Chief Minister. He said- I eat the salt and bread of the state, my family runs on the state's salary. If unparliamentary words are used against the head of that state, I will feel the pain. I too have a heart and sensitiveness. Because I am bound by UP Employee Rules. I couldn't bear this pain for two days, so I sent my resignation to the Governor." Earlier on Monday, the City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri of Bareilly had also resigned. The reason given was UGC's new law and the beating of Avimukteshwaranand's disciples. 'Cannot speak disrespectfully to CM while sitting on a handcart' The GST Deputy Commissioner said - I will continue my government work until my resignation is accepted. After the resignation is accepted, I will work for society with whatever means I have. Today, I am expressing the pain that I feel. The Constitution has defined ways to protest, but you cannot speak disrespectfully to the Chief Minister while sitting on a handcart. He is our provider. All I want to say is that you should be careful of such people. They create a wrong atmosphere in society. They divide society. I oppose such statements because they cause society to divide into castes. Know what has happened so far in the Avimukteshwaranand controversy

stories.title: 3 BJP leaders booked for intimidating rape survivor in Mau:Accused of pressuring her for compromise and offering money
stories.summary: A case was registered on Monday in Mau against three BJP leaders, including the party’s district vice-president, for allegedly intimidating a rape victim and pressuring her to compromise. The leaders had visited the victim’s house, where a video later surfaced showing them discussing a settlement. The victim alleged that the BJP leaders also offered money for a compromise and said she would not settle under any circumstances, insisting that the accused Ankit should either marry her or go to jail. Police have arrested the accused and registered an FIR against BJP district vice-president Santosh Kumar Singh alias Pannu, along with Kanhaiya Tiwari and Himanshu Rai. Case details Affair for 3 years, backed out on marriage Woman made a video of BJP leaders The victim alleges that after Ankit Singh went to jail, some local BJP leaders reached her house and started pressuring her to withdraw the case and compromise. During this, the victim made a video of the entire incident, which later went viral on social media. After the video surfaced, political activity in the district intensified. Based on the victim's complaint and the video, the police have registered a case against three BJP leaders under relevant sections. The accused include District Vice President Santosh Kumar Singh alias Pannu, Kanhaiya Tiwari, and Himanshu Rai. Additional Superintendent of Police Anoop Kumar said, When the victim was working on contract in the DUDA department, her colleague Ankit Singh had physical relations with her by promising marriage. A case was registered in this regard and the accused was sent to jail. Another complaint has now been filed by the victim, alleging that three people pressured her for a compromise. Police have registered a case in this matter and further legal action will be taken based on the evidence.

stories.title: Illegal Madrasas operating as schools on UP-Nepal border:Over 500 reopen after crackdown; sting reveals foreign funding, donations flowing through overseas links, networks
stories.summary: More than 500 madrasas that were declared illegal and shut down by the Uttar Pradesh government last year have quietly resumed operations along the sensitive UP–Nepal border region. An in-depth investigation has revealed that many of these institutions are now functioning under the cover of “private schools,” while continuing religious education without proper recognition or approval. The reopening of these Madrasas has raised serious concerns among security agencies and the local administration, especially after evidence surfaced showing that several of them are receiving foreign funds in the name of religious donations, particularly Zakat. The investigation shows how weak monitoring, legal loopholes, and local pressure have allowed these institutions to restart despite official orders. Massive crackdown in 2023 Between April and June 2023, the Uttar Pradesh government launched a large-scale crackdown on illegal madrasas operating near the UP–Nepal border. The action followed intelligence inputs and administrative surveys that flagged these institutions for running without registration, occupying government or Gram Sabha land, and lacking transparency in funding. During the operation, 542 Madrasas were sealed or demolished across districts like Siddharthnagar, Maharajganj, Shravasti, Balrampur, and Bahraich. Bulldozers were used at several locations where illegal construction was confirmed. Officials at the time said the action was necessary due to the sensitive nature of the border area and the lack of records regarding students, teachers, and funding sources. However, barely six to seven months later, many of these madrasas have resumed classes. How the Madrasas are reopening The investigation found that madrasa operators are using multiple methods to restart operations: While officially claiming to teach subjects like Hindi, English, Math, Science, and Geography, religious instruction continues alongside. Dhanora Buzurg: Madrasa running again In Dhanora Buzurg village of Siddharthnagar district, the madrasa Nurul Islam was found operating openly. Two teachers were seen teaching young children. A local resident, Abdul Ali, said, When the administration took action, the madrasa was closed. Later, officials told us we could reopen after completing paperwork. That is why it is still running. He added that the madrasa building is old and teachers come from nearby villages. At the village mosque, Karam Hussain, the muazzin, confirmed that funds are received from abroad, Many people from our village live in Saudi Arabia. They send money to their families, and the families give Zakat to the Madrasa. He further said, The Madrasa does not have recognition yet, but it will get it. We were given one year’s time. Foreign funding admitted on camera During the investigation, villagers and madrasa staff openly admitted that donations come from relatives working overseas. Karam Hussain said, Teachers are paid from donations and Zakat. Money comes through families whose relatives are in Saudi Arabia. He also claimed: SSB officers come to check what is being taught. We tell them we teach science and geography too. Hindu children also study here. Malgahia Village: Madrasa rebuilt elsewhere In Malgahia village, a large madrasa building near the mosque had been demolished during the government drive. Locals said hundreds of children studied there earlier. Now, classes are being held in another house. Madrasa manager Abdul Rashid said, The Madrasa was built on agricultural land. Later it was declared illegal and demolished. We had no place to teach, so we are trying to restart it elsewhere. Principal Maqbool Ahmed added, Our elders started this Madrasa in 1962, but it was never registered. That is why it was demolished. Now we are applying for school recognition. A local resident, Irshad Ahmed, leased his house for Madrasa use, I gave my house for 25 years at ₹1,000. Running a madrasa brings reward (Sawaab). Parsa Diwan: Madrasa runs despite closure In Parsa Diwan village, residents initially claimed that the madrasa had been shut. However, hidden-camera footage showed that classes were still being conducted. Teacher Maqsood Alam said, The Madrasa runs on village donations. Recognition has been stopped, so we don’t have it. He added that the madrasa operators live in Mumbai and teachers come from nearby villages. Shivbhari village: Demolition on Gram Sabha land In Shivbhari, a madrasa and mosque built on Gram Sabha land were demolished. Local resident Naseem said, Our land was wrongly recorded as wasteland. Because of this, the Madrasa was demolished. Before demolition, the madrasa had around 120 students. After closure, many children were enrolled in government schools, but parents complained about distance and lack of religious education. Villager Mujammil said, Poor families cannot send children far away. Their education has suffered. Dhanori village: Classes continue In Dhanori village, officials had earlier ordered the madrasa to obtain recognition. Despite this, classes continue six days a week. Teacher Ghulam Waris said, Officials visited 6–7 months ago and asked us to complete recognition. The process is ongoing. Sonauli border area: Court orders cited At the Sonauli border, 14 madrasas were shut during the drive. In Hardi Dali village, residents said the madrasa was sealed but later reopened. A villager, Ramzan, said, We were allowed to operate again through court orders. We are applying for school recognition and teaching other subjects as well. Mujhana milik: Large Madrasa still closed In Mujhana Milik village, a madrasa that once had 250 students remains closed. Teacher Fajre Alam said: We have filed a case in the High Court. If reopened, we will teach Hindi and English along with religious education. Why recognition is a major issue For years, recognition of madrasas in Uttar Pradesh has been stalled due to policy changes and legal challenges. As a result, many institutions continue without approval. Under education rules: However, many madrasa operators are now seeking school recognition to continue religious teaching indirectly. Government schools rejected by parents Many Muslim families prefer madrasa education because government schools do not provide religious instruction. Parents told investigators that: This demand keeps illegal madrasas running despite official bans. Officials warn of strict action Officials have made it clear that misuse of school recognition will not be allowed. Siddharthnagar District Inspector of Schools Arun Kumar said, Schools cannot teach religious subjects. If they do, recognition will be canceled. Maharajganj DIOS Pradeep Kumar Sharma said, Recognition will be given strictly as per rules. Religious education is not allowed in schools. Siddharthnagar SDM Vivekanand Mishra said: No Madrasa can run without recognition. If found, action will be taken. Nautanwa SDM Naveen Prasad added, Some institutions reopened due to court orders. Others operating illegally will face strict action.

stories.title: Uma Bharti backs Shankaracharya, slams administration for seeking proof:Avimukteshwaranand responds, she should convey this message to Yogi; officer resigns in support CM
stories.summary: The standoff between Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand and the Magh Mela administration has emerged as a serious problem for the government. BJP firebrand leader Uma Bharti has publicly backed Avimukteshwaranand, saying the administration crossed the limits of propriety by demanding proof from the Shankaracharya. Responding to her remarks, Avimukteshwaranand said she should convey the same message to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Blood letter sent to CM Yogi Dinesh Phalahari Baba, the main petitioner in the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi temple case, has written a letter in blood to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. He demanded that arrangements be made for Avimukteshwaranand to perform a Ganga bath with due respect. He also urged the Chief Minister to instruct officials to issue an apology. Dispute reaches bureaucracy The 10-day-long confrontation has now reached the bureaucracy. In Ayodhya, GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar Singh resigned in support of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. He said he was hurt by the abusive language allegedly used by Avimukteshwaranand against the Chief Minister and could no longer tolerate the insult. Calls for ban and NSA Meanwhile, Paramhans Maharaj of Ayodhya Cantonment Dham alleged that Avimukteshwaranand and Satua Baba had defamed the Magh Mela. He demanded that both be banned from entering the Magh Mela and called for the National Security Act (NSA) to be imposed on Avimukteshwaranand. City Magistrate’s resignation and strong remarks On Monday, Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri resigned in support of Avimukteshwaranand. Since then, the Shankaracharya has intensified his attacks on the government, saying the present battle was not between Hindus and Muslims or between the British and Indians, but between fake and real Hindus. What has happened so far ? On 18 January, Avimukteshwaranand was heading for a Mauni Amavasya bath in a palanquin when police stopped him and asked him to proceed on foot, leading to a scuffle with his disciples. The administration later issued two notices, questioning the use of the Shankaracharya title and the Mauni Amavasya disturbance, warning of a possible ban. After a Bareilly magistrate resigned on 26 January, his resignation was rejected, he was suspended, and an inquiry was ordered.

stories.title: Nathu La 1967, 4 soldiers and 1 officer:UP’s Attar Singh leads surviving jawans to halt Chinese assault, defends India’s pride
stories.summary: ‘UP ke Yoddha’ today tells the story of a soldier whose resolve held firm when an Indian post stood on the brink of collapse. During the 1967 Indo-China conflict, a forward post came under a sudden and intense enemy assault. Most soldiers stationed there were either killed or seriously wounded. Even in those conditions, 24-year-old Second Lieutenant Attar Singh refused to withdraw. With only four soldiers remaining, he held the position and stopped the enemy from advancing. For this act of leadership under fire, he received a rare field promotion to Captain. Attar Singh later played a key role in the 1971 war with Pakistan, where he was entrusted with sustaining Indian troops deep inside hostile desert terrain. Across both wars, his conduct became a lesson in composure, judgement and responsibility. But the defining chapter began in 1967. First posting on a tense frontier Attar Singh joined the Army as a soldier and was commissioned as a Second Lieutenant in the Grenadiers Regiment in 1967. His first posting was along the India-China border near Nathu La Pass. Even five years after the 1962 war, conditions on the frontier remained fragile. Chinese and Indian posts were separated by barely 50 yards. Soldiers faced each other daily, and confrontation was constant. On August 15, 1967, Attar Singh reported to his Company Commander, Captain Prithvi Singh Dagar. Assessing the young officer, Captain Dagar remarked that he was glad to have someone who could stand firm when required. Within days, Chinese soldiers began repeatedly crossing into Indian-held areas. Protests were met with intimidation. Army Headquarters ordered the installation of fencing to block further movement. Attar Singh assembled his platoon and began preparations. Border clashes and the fencing order As fencing work began, Chinese soldiers intervened, issuing threats and attempting to stop the activity. Verbal arguments quickly turned physical. Over the next two days, eight to nine such clashes took place. Captain Dagar reported the developments to higher command. The response was direct: reinforce the position and strengthen the fencing. Additional troops were rushed in. By evening, Indian strength at Nathu La had risen to nearly 350 soldiers under seven officers. Orders were issued to resume fencing at first light without hesitation. September 11, 1967: the battle at Nathu La At dawn, Indian soldiers took up their positions and resumed work. A small group of Chinese troops approached, signalling talks. Attar Singh warned that the gesture could not be trusted. Moments later, another Chinese unit emerged from cover and opened fire without warning. Machine guns, rifles and mortars were brought into action. The hills of Nathu La echoed with gunfire. What had begun as a confrontation turned into open battle. Indian troops were operating under restrictive orders. Heavy weapons required clearance from higher command. Despite determined resistance, casualties mounted rapidly. Two company commanders, including Captain Dagar, four Subedars and 83 soldiers were killed. Around 190 were seriously wounded. By late morning, Attar Singh was the senior surviving officer. Alone in command Radio communication had collapsed. Key weapon crews were injured. The cries of wounded soldiers filled the area. All of this unfolded within a range of 800–900 yards. Attar Singh now carried the full responsibility of the post. He had to ensure the evacuation of the wounded while preventing any enemy advance. By 11 am, only four soldiers remained with him. Realising the danger of exposure, Attar Singh devised a simple but effective tactic. He ordered the soldiers to fire from one position and immediately shift to another, repeating the process continuously. The objective was clear: the enemy must believe that Indian strength remained intact. The plan worked. Chinese troops hesitated, uncertain of the numbers facing them. Permission that changed the battle At around 2 pm, a signal line was partially restored. Attar Singh contacted Brigadier Ray Singh Yadav and briefed him on the situation. The instruction was firm: the post was not to be abandoned. Soon after, Major General Sagat Singh intervened and authorised artillery fire, accepting full responsibility for the decision. Indian guns opened up. The enemy’s forward positions collapsed. Chinese forces suffered heavy losses, estimated at around 450 killed, and withdrew from the area. The battle marked a decisive shift and restored confidence lost in 1962. The next morning, Attar Singh was summoned. In recognition of his conduct, he was promoted directly to Captain—an advancement that normally takes several years. The 1971 war: leadership in the desert During the 1971 war with Pakistan, Captain Attar Singh was posted to Rajasthan’s Barmer sector. The terrain offered no roads, little water and extreme conditions. He was assigned a critical logistical role: delivering food, water and ammunition to Indian troops advancing inside Pakistani territory. With the Army’s focus on Punjab and East Pakistan, the Rajasthan front posed unique challenges. Using old railway tracks as guides, Attar Singh led a convoy of 16 vehicles across shifting sand. Iron sheets were placed under tyres to prevent vehicles from sinking. After 28 hours of continuous effort, supplies reached the front, eight kilometres across open desert. When informed that a platoon had gone without food and water for two days, Attar Singh immediately diverted camel-borne supplies to their position. Life at the front Conditions were severe. Soldiers were rationed one litre of water per day. Bathing was rare. Water was reused for washing clothes. Even so, operations continued. Indian forces advanced nearly 78 kilometres inside Pakistan, holding their ground through discipline and planning. When an entire platoon came close to destruction One night, while moving without lights in enemy territory, Attar Singh noticed movement ahead and ordered the convoy to halt. Moments later, an order to fire tank shells at close range was heard. Recognising the voice, Attar Singh called out to Major R.D. Law, his former instructor at the Indian Military Academy. The firing order was cancelled instantly. Eight tanks stood ready. Seconds more would have meant the destruction of the entire convoy. Presence of mind and recognition saved the platoon. A soldier’s career After 32 years of service, Attar Singh retired in 1992 with the rank of Colonel. stories.title: Weather shift in UP; hailstorm hits Baghpat:Heavy rain in Ghaziabad–Agra, dust storm covers Mathura
stories.summary: Weather conditions may change again across Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday. The Meteorological Department has issued a hail alert for 14 districts and a thunderstorm alert for 50 districts. Officials say that if hail occurs, temperatures could drop by 3–4 degrees Celsius. Most districts began the day with clear skies, but strong winds continue to intensify the chill. People were seen gathering around bonfires in several areas to cope with the cold. Muzaffarnagar remained the coldest district in the state, recording a minimum temperature of 5.1 degrees Celsius. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said that due to the impact of a western disturbance, parts of western UP may receive rain today, with wind speeds reaching 30–40 kmph at some locations. See the weather pictures - Now know the conditions of big cities New disturbance will be active after 3 days The Meteorological Department said the influence of westerly winds continues across North India. Wind circulation remains active over Haryana and adjoining regions, while a strong westerly jet stream is flowing at higher altitudes. A new western disturbance is likely to affect north-west India from the night of January 30, which may bring further changes in weather conditions. Zero visibility recorded in Saharanpur–Prayagraj in 24 hours In the last 24 hours, zero visibility was recorded in Saharanpur and Prayagraj, disrupting traffic movement. No significant change was observed in daytime temperatures across the state. Temperatures remained well above normal in Gorakhpur division, while Ayodhya and Lucknow divisions recorded slightly above-normal readings. At night, temperatures rose in Gorakhpur division but dropped sharply in Ayodhya division. Minimum temperatures were much above normal in Varanasi division, while Bareilly and Agra divisions recorded below-normal levels. Other divisions remained near normal. How will the weather be for 3 days January 28: Light rain possible; cloudy skies; temperatures likely to fall. January 29: Thunderstorms with drizzle in western UP; light rain likely in eastern UP. January 30: Light rain possible with thunderstorms; strong winds likely in some areas.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan confirms bid for 2029 Lok Sabha polls:BJP leader alleges ‘international conspiracy’ behind wrestlers’ allegations, backs Vinay Katiyar’s first claim on Ayodhya
stories.summary: BJP senior leader and six-time MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has said that the Rashtra Katha was organised to unite different castes of society and link the ideals of Lord Ram with freedom fighters such as Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Chandrashekhar Azad. Alleging an international conspiracy involving Khalistani elements and the Congress behind the women wrestlers’ case, he said he would definitely contest the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, with the party deciding the seat. He made these remarks in a special conversation with Bhaskar Digital, during which he also spoke on Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Akhilesh Yadav, Pankaj Chaudhary and future politics... Question: Will you contest from Ayodhya? Vinay Katiyar has also spoken about contesting from there. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: No. I recently went to Barabanki, where I was asked the same question. I want to say clearly through your platform that Vinay Katiyar has the first right over the Ayodhya Lok Sabha seat. He should contest, and I welcome that. Question: You have said you want to go to the Lok Sabha once more. Why? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: I do not wish to be woven into a maiden’s jewellery. I have been an MP six times. My wife was once an MP, my son is an MP, and many associates have become MLAs and MPs. I have no such personal ambition. However, I believe there was a conspiracy against me in 2023–24. Because of that, I said I would like to return to the Lok Sabha. I am saying it again today. I will contest in 2029. The seat will be decided later. Question: Which seat will you contest from? Your son is an MP from Kaiserganj. Are you looking at another seat? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: The party knows everything. The party will decide from where I should contest. Question: What if the party says your son should contest again? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: I want to go to the Lok Sabha once, by any means. Question: Who was behind the allegations made by women wrestlers in 2023? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: This was a worldwide conspiracy. I said then that I would come out unblemished, and I am saying it again today. Congress leaders were the most visible at the protest sites. Priyanka Gandhi, Ashok Gehlot and Bhupinder Hooda were involved. But it was not limited to them. Many others tried to take advantage of the situation. Some people from our own side were also involved. There was support from Khalistani elements as well. Banners and posters were put up even in the United States. Question: You were facing serious allegations. How much support did you get from the party? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: What crisis? Allegations alone do not create a crisis. My party gave me full support. Question: Meetings of MLAs from specific communities were held in Lucknow. How do you see this? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: Such meetings should happen. Similar meetings also take place inside Parliament. Representatives from all parties belonging to a particular community attend them. They discuss issues and convey them to their respective parties. There is nothing wrong in people from the same community meeting and sharing concerns. The problem arises only if they come out and speak against the party. In my view, issuing a notice over such meetings was wrong. Question: BJP suffered setbacks in 2024. What does your experience say about 2027? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: It is too early to say. Elections are still far away. As of now, BJP appears strong. Question: There has been discussion about your relationship with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: Our relationship was never bad. There was a phase when we did not meet. When he called, I went. We have known each other since childhood. When Gurudev Avaidyanath Maharaj was alive, I used to visit the temple regularly. He never treated me any differently from Yogi ji. Question: What are your views on SIR, as many names have reportedly been removed? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: This is a serious issue. People should show patience. It needs proper study. Some matters are before the Supreme Court. There is pressure on us to comment, but until I am clear about what is right and wrong, I do not think it is appropriate to speak. Question: Have you met BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: Not yet. He has been travelling extensively, and I was busy with religious discourse. We spoke over the phone. He has been attending our katha for 25 years. The party has made him president after due consideration. We were elected to the Lok Sabha together in 1991. Today, he is a Union minister. His appointment will benefit the party. Question: Were you invited to the Ayodhya temple consecration ceremony? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: When I was not invited, I did not go. When I was invited, I attended. Question: What was the objective behind organising Rashtra Katha? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: Hindu society is divided into many castes. Over time, divisions have deepened. Through Rashtra Katha, the aim was to bring everyone together. The event was inaugurated by 52 religious leaders from different castes. It was not organised for personal publicity. The story included Ram, Hanuman, Subhas Chandra Bose and Chandrashekhar Azad. It addressed national issues and created awareness among students and society. Question: Akhilesh Yadav often praises you and even offered you a ticket in 2024. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: I also praise Akhilesh. He is a good person. We share an old relationship. We respected Mulayam Singh Yadav’s working style, even when political relations were strained. Question: What do you think about Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA slogan? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: That is his agenda. I have nothing to do with it. Question: Do you watch films? Have you watched Border 2? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: I watch films regularly. I have not watched Border 2 yet. I prefer watching South Indian films, as they focus on history and culture. Question: You own a helicopter, horses and luxury vehicles. How do you prefer to travel? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: I am a man of the ground. I prefer travelling by car. Question: What are the chances of Prateek becoming a minister in the UP cabinet? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: I do not see that possibility. Such decisions are taken by the organisation and the government. Question: Have you been given any responsibility for the upcoming three-tier elections? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: Last time, I was given responsibility in five districts, and we succeeded. Whether I will be given responsibility again is for the party to decide. Question: You reacted strongly when compared to Raja Bhaiya. Why? Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh: Such comparisons are driven by social media trends. They create unnecessary conflict among supporters. Raja Bhaiya has his own political standing and history. Comparing leaders in this way serves no purpose and harms society.

stories.title: Four die as car rams into truck on Delhi-Mumbai Expressway:Vehicle dragged for 8 km, family returning to Noida after Mahakal darshan
stories.summary: A speeding car rammed into the back of a truck on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway in Dausa. Four people in the car died in the accident, while one young man was seriously injured. The car was severely stuck under the truck, causing it to be dragged along for some distance. The bodies were also trapped inside the car, and the police had to struggle to extricate them. The accident occurred near pillar number 193 of the expressway in the Paparda area on Tuesday morning at around 5:30 AM. All the deceased were young men from Noida. The car was completely wrecked, making it difficult to extract the bodies. PHOTOS from the accident... DSP Deepak Meena said that a car with a Haryana license plate was traveling from Lalsot (Dausa) towards Delhi. Near Aluda village, the car crashed into a truck ahead of it. Due to the high speed, the car got stuck under the back of the truck. The front of the car was completely destroyed, and the occupants were trapped inside. Police and the expressway's rescue team arrived at the scene. After considerable effort, the car was separated from the truck, and the bodies were removed. According to eyewitnesses, the truck driver did not immediately realize the accident had occurred. As a result, the car was dragged along with the truck. The car's occupants had no chance of survival. There were five people in the car. The injured young man has been admitted to the district hospital in Dausa. The police have placed the bodies in the mortuary. Their identities have not yet been established. The car traveled from one police station area to another Constable Mahesh of Paparda police station said that all the occupants of the car were returning to Noida after visiting the Mahakal temple in Ujjain. After crashing into the truck in the Rahuwas police station area, the speeding car got stuck. The car was then dragged into the Paparda police station area. Traffic on the expressway was affected for some time after the accident. Traffic was restored after the damaged vehicles were removed.

stories.title: UP plans Shiksha Mitra pay hike:Yogi government’s fifth budget likely to focus on women, pensioners ahead of 2027 polls
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government’s fifth budget, to be presented in February, is expected to carry a strong welfare push aimed at women and socially vulnerable groups, as the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) sharpens its strategy for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. According to sources, the government is preparing to extend financial benefits to more than one crore women through proposed hikes in pensions and honorariums. The focus is on increasing old age pension, destitute women pension, widow pension, disability pension, as well as incentives for ASHA workers and honorarium for Shiksha Mitras. Political analysts view these moves as part of a broader effort to consolidate a vote bank that not only votes in large numbers but also plays a decisive role in shaping opinion at the village and neighbourhood level. Budget seen as key tool for electoral mobilisation With the 2027 elections still over a year away, the government has already begun aligning its budgetary priorities with political objectives. The past two days of political activity underline this shift. Union Home Minister Amit Shah recently hinted at the election timeline during the UP Day programme, while BJP national president Nitin Navin urged party workers in Mathura to begin preparations for 2027. Together, these developments signal that electoral groundwork has formally begun. For Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, retaining power for a third consecutive term remains the central challenge. Women voters played a decisive role in the BJP’s victories in the 2017 Assembly elections, the 2019 Lok Sabha polls, and the 2022 Assembly elections. The party has replicated this strategy in states such as Haryana, Maharashtra, Delhi and Bihar by announcing women-centric welfare schemes. Talks underway on pension and honorarium hikes Sources in the finance department say discussions have already taken place between Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Finance Minister Suresh Khanna and Additional Chief Secretary (Finance) Deepak Kumar on increasing pension amounts for the elderly, destitute women and persons with disabilities. There is also a “principled agreement” to enhance incentives for ASHA workers and the honorarium paid to Shiksha Mitras. Budgetary calculations for these increases are currently underway. Honorarium hike likely for 1.47 lakh Shiksha Mitras After nearly nine years, the government is considering an increase in the honorarium of Shiksha Mitras. Around 1.47 lakh Shiksha Mitras and more than 28,000 instructors could benefit from the proposal. The key question under discussion is whether the honorarium should be increased by Rs 2,000 per month or more. The BJP had promised a legal solution to the Shiksha Mitra issue in its 2017 manifesto, but their adjustment as assistant teachers was later struck down by the Supreme Court. In 2017, the Yogi government had increased their honorarium from Rs 3,500 to Rs 10,000 per month. No revision has taken place since then, despite repeated demands from both ruling party and opposition legislators. Recently, Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh also hinted at a possible increase. Pension hike for elderly, women and disabled persons At present, 67.50 lakh elderly people in Uttar Pradesh receive an old age pension of Rs 1,000 per month, paid quarterly. The finance department is considering increasing this amount to Rs 1,500 per month. If approved, this would be the third hike under the Yogi government, following increases in 2019 and 2022. Under the destitute women pension scheme, 38.58 lakh women currently receive Rs 1,000 per month. This amount is also proposed to be raised to Rs 1,500. Similarly, around 11.98 lakh persons with disabilities receive a monthly pension of Rs 1,000. The government is preparing to increase this to Rs 1,500 per month. ASHA workers and leprosy patients also to benefit Uttar Pradesh has nearly 1.70 lakh ASHA workers, considered the backbone of the rural healthcare system. They currently receive incentive payments ranging between Rs 2,500 and Rs 3,500 per month. A proposal to increase this incentive is under consideration. In addition, 13,395 leprosy patients who currently receive a monthly pension of Rs 3,000 may see this rise to between Rs 3,500 and Rs 4,000. Government targets one crore women beneficiaries Officials estimate that women form the majority of beneficiaries across most welfare schemes. Of the 67.50 lakh old age pension recipients, around 40 lakh are women. The destitute women pension scheme covers over 38 lakh women, while nearly five lakh women benefit from the disability pension scheme. Added to this are more than 1.60 lakh ASHA workers. Senior journalist and political analyst Virendra Nath Bhatt says pension hikes are often justified on inflation grounds, but political considerations cannot be ignored. “The government and the BJP have clearly begun election preparations. The upcoming budget is likely to contain populist announcements for every major social group,” he said. Former Additional Chief Secretary (Finance) Sanjeev Mittal noted that strong revenue collections from GST, VAT, excise, transport, and stamp and registration have given the government fiscal space. “When revenues are healthy, governments tend to increase spending on welfare schemes. Such spending also yields political dividends,” he said.

stories.title: Have Brahmin MPs tied ghungroos? asks Alankar Agnihotri:Bareilly city magistrate calls situation like civil war, warns generations will blame today’s silence
stories.summary: Bareilly City Magistrate Alankar Agnihotri, a PCS officer from the Brahmin community, resigned on Monday, expressing anger over what he described as an insult to Shankaracharya and the new UGC law. Agnihotri questioned, “Do you want the genocide of Brahmins? I want to ask Brahmin MPs and MLAs, will you remain silent even when sisters and daughters are raped on the streets? What bells have you worn, and when will you speak? Who was the Prayagraj DM cooking bread for? Is he a Shankaracharya?” He cited both the UGC’s new law and the assault on disciples of Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand as key reasons for his resignation. Dainik Bhaskar conducted a special interview with him following the announcement. Read the full conversation... Question: Why did you suddenly resign? Answer: For some time now, the situations that have developed in the state are going from bad to worse. A campaign is being run against a particular class, especially Brahmins, which has now become unbearable. Sometimes, bulldozers run over someone's house, and sometimes people are beaten to death in police stations. In jail, a deputy jailer killed a disabled person and another Brahmin. The most tragic incident is from the Prayagraj Magh Mela. The disciples of Avimukteshwaranand Maharaj were grabbed by their tuft (shikha) and beaten up. Such videos have emerged that make one's soul tremble. When administration officials themselves treat revered saints and their disciples this way, what message will it send to society? Is this preparation for the genocide of Brahmins? What do they want to achieve? Question: Are you questioning the current system? Answer: You say that he is not Shankaracharya at all. What do you want to say? Are those who are roaming around in big cars Shankaracharya? You are giving them VIP treatment. Your officials are taking photos with them. Your officials are warming up with them. Which Shankaracharya are they? Why is the administration doing so much flattery? The DM of Prayagraj is warming up with them. What authority does he have to warm up there? Nothing happened to them. On one hand, the disciples of the real Shankaracharya are being beaten, on the other hand, top administrative officials are sitting with some so-called saints, warming up and getting photos taken. Has the administration now become a hub of sycophancy? Our revered ones are being insulted. Those who are close to power are being given VIP treatment. Why this double standard? Question: What is your objection regarding UGC Regulation 2026? Answer: This regulation (January 13, 2026) is extremely discriminatory. It treats meritorious students from the general category as 'self-declared criminals'. They cannot be discriminated against. There is a high possibility of mental and physical exploitation of children through equality committees. Anyone can file a baseless complaint and ruin someone's future. Will we send our children to study in such a system where exploitation happens in the name of justice? I also want to ask those public representatives who take votes in the name of the Brahmin society and today sit silently like 'corporate employees'. Do you want the genocide of Brahmins? I want to ask MPs and MLAs - why are you wearing ankle bells, when will you speak up? Are you people waiting for our daughters and daughters-in-law to be raped on the streets? Are you waiting for orders from your masters? Will you speak only when the situation gets out of hand? You took tickets in the name of Brahmins. You took votes from Brahmins. Once you win, it doesn't matter anymore. Question: How do you see the future situation? Answer: Today, where is the upper caste society safe? Look at social media, across the country, the general category has separated from you. Both the central government and state government are minority governments. Today, neither democracy nor republic remains; this is just an 'illusion system'. Governments are in the minority and are running only on the policy of 'divide and rule'. BJP is no longer Indian; it has become like a 'Foreign People's Party'. I have resigned for this reason so that a message goes out that the general category is no longer with you. I have sent my resignation to the Governor, District Magistrate, and Election Commission (as ERO). Question: What do you want now? Answer: I am taking this step with Lord Bajrangbali as my witness. Now is the time for society and officials to boycott this injustice like a 'non-cooperation movement'. If we don't wake up today, future generations will never forgive us. The situation has become like a civil war. The future strategy will be decided by our Brahmin community's MLAs, MPs, and our society on what needs to be done next. That's why I have done this with Lord Bajrangbali as my witness. Now know about Alankar Agnihotri Alankar Agnihotri is from Kanpur. His father passed away in his childhood. Mother worked in a bank. In 1998, Alankar secured 21st rank in UP Board's 12th examination. After this, he completed B.Tech from Banaras Hindu University and started working. In 2014, when all of Alankar's younger brothers were settled, and his sister was married, he quit his job to prepare for the UPPCS and qualified for the exam in 2019.

stories.title: Wife kills husband with sons in Lucknow:Brother says man is beaten with sticks, body crushed and thrown 1 KM from home
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a 50-year-old man was beaten to death by his wife and sons. His body was found in a pit about 1 km from his home on Tuesday morning, after locals informed the police. The deceased was identified as Arjun Pal. The police have taken his wife and sons into custody based on a complaint by the deceased’s brother. He alleged that they attacked Arjun Pal with sticks and rods and then dumped his body in the pit to make it look like an accident. The incident happened in Kharta village, under Malihabad police station. Seeing a body in the pit, the police were informed Local people saw a body in a pit near the Nabinagar canal bridge in the Malihabad police station area on Tuesday morning around 10 AM. Local people informed the police about it. When the police, who arrived on receiving the information, started investigating, the deceased was identified as Arjun Pal, a resident of Kharta village. The deceased's brother, Munnu Lal, said- I immediately reached the spot upon receiving the information. An e-rickshaw was lying on top of my brother Arjun Pal's body. There were injury marks on his face. Also, nearby, a steel tank and a blood-stained bed were lying. Wife and sons killed the brother Based on my suspicion and for investigation, the police also reached brother Arjun Pal's house. There, bloodstains were found in the room. Arjun's wife and both sons crushed his face and murdered him. To make this murder look like an accident, the body was thrown into a pit about 1 kilometer away from the house. An e-rickshaw was dropped on top of it. Seen going by e-rickshaw at 3 AM Brother Munnu Lal said that Arjun's two sons are addicted to alcohol and gambling. Late on Monday night, both sons had assaulted their father Arjun Pal. According to villagers, an e-rickshaw was seen leaving the village around 3 AM on Tuesday night, but due to darkness, the people inside could not be identified. Malihabad Inspector Surendra Singh Bhati said that based on the brother's complaint, the wife and both sons have been taken into custody. Initial investigation suggests that the body was taken by e-rickshaw and dumped to make it look like an accident. Bloodstains have been found in both the room and the e-rickshaw. We are investigating from all angles.

stories.title: If Aparna divorces, will BJP openly back her?:Mulayam family daughter-in-law identity becomes key factor; putting her political future at stake now
stories.summary: BJP leader Aparna Yadav and Prateek Yadav, the younger brother of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, are heading towards separation. On Monday, Prateek Yadav announced on Instagram that he will divorce Aparna. After this announcement, many questions have come up in political circles. People are asking what stand the BJP will take if the marriage ends, how much support the party will give Aparna, and whether her political future is in danger. Political experts say Aparna’s main political identity comes from being the daughter-in-law of Mulayam Singh Yadav and the wife of Akhilesh Yadav’s brother. The BJP has also gained at times by using her to target the Samajwadi Party. If the divorce happens, analysts believe it could have a big impact on her political career. Read the full report... BJP made Aparna the face against SP Being the daughter-in-law of the Mulayam family is Aparna's USP Political analyst Yogesh Mishra believes - Aparna Yadav Bisht's only USP is being the daughter-in-law of the Mulayam Singh family. Aparna herself is the daughter of a Thakur family from Uttarakhand. In BJP, there are many Thakur women office bearers from the women's wing to the main body. But, Aparna is being promoted only because she is the wife of Akhilesh's brother Prateek Yadav. If their relationship does not remain, Aparna will face difficulties on the social and political front. Political future may be at stake Political analyst Anil Singh believes that if Aparna and Prateek Yadav break their marriage, it will directly affect Aparna's political life. If her relationship with the Yadav family breaks, BJP will not be able to make her a face against SP. Even within the party, her opponents will raise the issue. They will say that when Aparna has no relation with the Yadav family, why should she be made a face? Anyway, Aparna's future in BJP does not look very bright, because she is not a mass leader. Her image as a leader is also not appealing. BJP can also make divorce an issue A section of political experts believes that this can be made an issue to gain women's sympathy for Aparna. The party can strategically attack Prateek, questioning how he made posts defaming his wife on social media? Under its guise, the party can also corner SP. If this happens, it can once again use Aparna against Saifai's Yadav family. Aparna was a contender for the mayoral post Aparna had staked her claim for the mayoral post in the 2023 Lucknow Municipal Corporation elections. Many RSS and BJP leaders, from Lucknow to Delhi, were advocating for her. However, the Lucknow mayoral ticket was to be decided by Defense Minister Rajnath Singh. According to sources, Aparna Yadav did not meet Rajnath Singh's criteria. Prior to this, Aparna had also claimed tickets from Lucknow Cantt and Sarojini Nagar in 2022. In 2022, there were also speculations that the BJP might field her as a candidate against Akhilesh. But that didn't happen either. Had joined the Women's Commission with great difficulty Aparna Yadav was not happy about getting the post of Vice President in the State Women's Commission. She wanted at least the President's post. Annoyed at getting the Vice President's post, Aparna did not join for a few days. After that, she took charge of the post after discussions with the then BJP State President Bhupendra Chaudhary and CM Yogi.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav asks SP MPs to monitor voter roll revision:Calls for FIRs, court action over wrongful deletions; warns against BJP interference
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday briefed party MPs at a meeting in Lucknow, asking them to work seriously on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in their districts. He told MPs to help restore the names of voters whose entries were deleted and to remain alert to any disturbance by the BJP. If irregularities are found, he said, FIRs must be filed, and courts approached if police refuse to register cases. Rajya Sabha MPs also attended the meeting at the SP office. Discussions covered SIR, preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections, the BJP’s strategy, candidate selection and coordination with Congress. Senior leaders, including Dimple Yadav, Ram Gopal Yadav and Ramji Lal Suman, were present. Read what the MPs present in the meeting said MPs share feedback Chandauli MP Virendra Singh said a resolution was taken to form a PDA government in 2027, with a focus on social justice and clear strategy. MPs submitted district-wise SIR reports and were asked to strengthen party organisation locally. Jaunpur MP Babu Singh Kushwaha said the party would build booth-level strength and accused the BJP of insulting Hindu saints, including Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand. Kaushambi MP Pushpendra Saroj alleged officials were being pressured to add fake votes through SIR. He said FIRs would be filed and legal remedies pursued if needed. Sambhal MP Ziaur Rahman Barq said the party would work unitedly for the elections, raise public issues and oppose any unfair deletion of voters’ names. He said SP was not against SIR, but against wrongful cuts. What Akhilesh Yadav said Akhilesh Yadav asked MPs to recommend Assembly candidates who are active on the ground, influential and capable of taking on the BJP. He warned against factionalism and said the sole goal must be forming the party’s government in 2027. He claimed there were major discrepancies between voter lists used by different election bodies and alleged attempts to manipulate SIR. He accused the BJP government of undermining the Constitution, misusing public funds and insulting various social groups. He said district-level manifestos would be prepared based on local issues. Akhilesh also alleged attacks on Sanatan culture and the rights of PDA communities, and accused the BJP of tampering with reservation policies.

stories.title: UPESSC announces new dates for TET-TGT, PGT:Exam calendar released, recruitment tests scheduled between April and July across Uttar Pradesh this year
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission (UPESSC) on Tuesday announced fresh dates for the TET, TGT, PGT and Assistant Professor recruitment examinations, bringing relief to lakhs of candidates who have been waiting for clarity for months. The decision was taken in a meeting chaired by Commission Chairman Dr Prashant Kumar. According to an official notification issued on January 20, 2026, the examinations for Assistant Professor, Post Graduate Teacher (PGT), Trained Graduate Teacher (TGT) and the Uttar Pradesh Teacher Eligibility Test (UP TET) will be conducted on different dates between April and July 2026. Exam schedule released As per the examination calendar released by the commission: The commission stated that all examinations will be conducted with strict adherence to security norms, transparency and fairness. Earlier postponed exam rescheduled UPESSC clarified that the Assistant Professor exam ( No. 51), which was earlier scheduled for April 16 and 17, 2025, had been postponed due to administrative reasons. The commission has now decided to conduct the exam afresh in April 2026. Details regarding exam centres, shifts and admit cards will be shared separately with candidates in due course. Applications and information on official website The commission said that subject-wise application details and the complete examination notification for Assistant Professor recruitment will be made available on the official UPESSC website. A separate will also be issued for UP TET 2026, inviting online applications from eligible candidates. Candidates step up preparations With the release of the exam calendar, lakhs of aspirants have intensified their preparation. Candidates who have been awaiting recruitment for a long time expressed relief and optimism following the announcement. The commission has advised applicants to rely only on the official website for updates and avoid misinformation. UP TET last held in January 2022 The UP TET examination was last conducted on January 21, 2022, after the earlier test scheduled for November 28, 2021, was cancelled due to a paper leak. Since then, the exam had not been held, leaving a large number of aspirants waiting. The commission had earlier announced dates for UP TET on January 29 and 30, 2025, but the process stalled following the resignation of then chairperson Prof Kirti Pandey. Delays in appointing a new chairman further postponed the exam. After Prashant Kumar assumed charge as chairman, the decision was taken in his very first meeting. Supreme Court ruling makes TET mandatory On September 1, 2025, the Supreme Court, while hearing petitions related to the mandatory requirement of TET for teaching jobs in Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra, ruled that teachers with more than five years of service remaining must qualify the Teacher Eligibility Test. The bench comprising Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih said that failure to clear TET would result in resignation or compulsory retirement. Following this verdict, around 10 lakh teachers nationwide, including nearly 2 lakh in Uttar Pradesh, were affected. The court also noted that whether the ruling would apply to minority institutions would be decided by a larger bench later.

'RSS and BJP want to abolish constitution': Congress leader says, 'Modi wants to starve poor and divert country’s wealth to industrialists Ambani and Adani' Congress leader Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that the BJP-led government is deliberately weakening welfare schemes to benefit industrialists like Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani on Tuesday. The announcement was made today at the party headquarters in Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed him by garlanding him at the event. 5. stories.title: Son killed parents, wife daughter in Etah:Daughter’s wedding was 20 days away; 5-year-old boy lights 4 funeral pyres
stories.summary: In a shocking case that has stunned the district, a medicine trader has been arrested for brutally murdering four members of his own family-his elderly parents, wife and daughter-inside their two-storey home in broad daylight. Police say the accused, Kamal Singh, strangled the victims one by one and then crushed their heads with an interlocking brick in an attempt to ensure death and mislead investigators by staging the crime as a robbery. The murders allegedly stemmed from mounting tension over his daughter’s upcoming wedding and the inability to arrange sufficient money for the ceremony scheduled on February 11. 4 bodies from the same family arrived, women unconscious, see pictures... Murder Unfolded Over Family Dispute According to DIG Prabhakar Chaudhary of Aligarh Range, Kamal Singh’s 20-year-old daughter Jyoti was due to be married next month. Financial stress related to wedding preparations led to frequent arguments between Kamal and his wife, Ratna Devi (45). On Monday afternoon, an argument escalated violently. In a fit of rage, Kamal allegedly strangled his wife to death. When daughter Jyoti rushed in after hearing the commotion, she too was killed. Moments later, Kamal’s elderly parents—Ganga Singh (75) and Shyama Devi (70)—witnessed the horrific scene and were also murdered to eliminate witnesses. Police say all four victims were first strangled and then brutally attacked with an interlocking brick, crushing their heads and faces. CCTV Footage Exposes the Crime Investigators say CCTV footage played a key role in breaking the case. One camera shows Kamal arriving home on his motorcycle around 1 pm for lunch. At that time, everything appeared normal and there were no signs of robbery or disturbance. Another clip shows him leaving the house later on his bike. Police believe the murders were committed in the time window between Kamal’s departure and the return of his school-going son at 2 pm. Authorities say Kamal tried to give the impression of a robbery, but the absence of stolen items and forensic evidence quickly pointed towards an inside job. Bodies Discovered by Son Returning From School The crime came to light when Kamal’s minor son returned home from school. The fan was running upstairs despite the cold weather, raising suspicion. When he received no response to his calls, he went inside and discovered the blood-soaked bodies. A blood-stained interlocking brick was found near the victims, and Shyama Devi was reportedly still breathing when police arrived, but she succumbed to her injuries shortly afterwards. Postmortem Confirms Brutal Killings A panel of three doctors—Dr Rajeev Kishore, Dr Utsav Jain and Dr Shweta Rajput—conducted the postmortem examinations. Their report confirmed that all four deaths were the result of brutal homicide, not accidental or natural causes. Doctors noted severe injuries to the head, face and nose of the victims. The report concluded that strangulation was followed by repeated blows with a heavy brick to ensure death. According to medical findings, the sequence of murder was: first the wife, then the daughter, followed by the elderly mother. The father was killed separately on the ground floor. Crime Scene Layout Reveals Sequence Police reconstructed the crime scene based on body positions: The layout supported the prosecution’s claim of a calculated, sequential attack. Wedding Tensions and Love Affair Angle Family members revealed that Jyoti worked in Noida and was allegedly involved in a love affair with a man from a Saxena family in Chandigarh. Despite this, the family was proceeding with an arranged marriage, which further intensified domestic tensions. Relatives said disputes over wedding expenses and preparations had become frequent in recent weeks. Police are investigating whether this emotional and financial pressure served as the immediate trigger for the murders. Final Rites Performed by Five-Year-Old Son Scenes turned heart-wrenching on Tuesday when the bodies arrived home after postmortem. Women in the neighbourhood broke down in grief as all four bodies were taken for last rites under heavy police security. The most disturbing moment came when five-year-old Devansh, the only surviving male family member, performed the final rites at four funeral pyres simultaneously, lighting the pyres of his grandparents, mother and elder sister. Police Investigation and Official Statements Senior officials including ADG Anupama Kulshrestha and DIG Prabhakar Chaudhary visited the spot. CCTV footage has been seized, forensic evidence collected, and multiple police teams deployed. Initially, police suspected multiple attackers or an outsider, but evidence eventually pointed towards Kamal Singh himself, who has now been arrested. “Evidence has been collected and the accused is in custody. The case will be solved conclusively,” ADG Kulshrestha said. The incident has left the entire area in shock, raising disturbing questions about domestic pressure, financial stress and hidden violence within families.

stories.title: PCS aspirant found dead in Prayagraj hostel:2 male students entered girls hostel, removed body from noose; fled after leaving her at hospital
stories.summary: A 25 year old woman, who was preparing for the PCS exam in Prayagraj, was found hanging in a girls’ hostel late at night. Two young men reached the hostel around midnight and took her down from the noose. They then took her to Beli Hospital. Doctors at the hospital declared her dead. After this, the two young men left her body there and fled. The incident created panic, and the police reached the hospital and the hostel soon after. The deceased student was identified as Riya Pandey. Riya is the daughter of Sushil Kumar Pandey, a resident of Antamau Manikpur Pratapgarh. Riya was preparing for PCS while staying in the girls' hostel. The entire incident took place around 1 AM on Monday night in the Cantt police station area. Had been living in the hostel for two months Riya Pandey had been preparing for competitive exams for 4 years while staying in the hostel. Before this, she used to live in a rented house. It had only been two months since Riya came to Rajapur Hostel. She was the second of three sisters. She has a brother named Adarsh Pandey. Adarsh Pandey was informed about the matter by another student living in the same hostel.

stories.title: Court convicts tuition-teacher, lover friend in 'Kushagra Murder Case':Mother demands hanging; murder plot created 26 months ago
stories.summary: In one of Kanpur’s most shocking kidnapping-murder cases, the court on Tuesday held all three accused guilty in the Kushagra Kanodia murder. Tuition teacher Rachita Vats, her lover Prabhat Shukla and his friend Aryan Gupta alias Shiva were convicted by the court. While the accused have been found guilty, the quantum of punishment will be pronounced on January 22. Victim's mother demands death penalty for killers As the order was read out, Kushagra’s mother broke down in court, demanding the death penalty for her son’s killers. Today's 3 pictures... Court proceedings and Prosecution case Kushagra’s disappearance on October 30 Murder inside Prabhat’s house Under the pretext of showing something, Prabhat took Kushagra to a storage-like room outside his house and strangled him to death. At the time of murder, Prabhat’s friend Aryan Gupta alias Shiva was standing guard outside the room. After killing Kushagra, the accused began executing the next phase of their plan. Ransom letter to mislead investigation After the murder, Prabhat and Shiva went to Kushagra’s house on Rachita’s scooter and threw a ransom letter demanding ₹30 lakh. To divert the investigation, they deliberately wrote “Allah Hu Akbar” in the letter and used religious references to create confusion. While throwing the letter, the apartment guard Rajendra noticed the scooter. On closer inspection, he found that the number plate had been tampered with by changing ‘F’ to ‘E’ using black tape. The scooter belonged to Rachita Vats. Family reaches Rachita’s house, body recovered Guard Rajendra informed Kushagra’s mother Sonia Kanodia, about the scooter. The family rushed to Rachita’s house, where she appeared nervous and claimed innocence, saying Prabhat had taken her scooter. With police assistance, the family reached Indrakuti Hata, where Kushagra’s body was recovered from the room outside Prabhat’s house. During interrogation, Rachita confessed that she wanted to marry Prabhat and had planned the kidnapping for ransom to become wealthy. Planning began on Kushagra’s birthday Car booking and call records Police revealed that before the incident, Rachita and Prabhat had even finalised a new car at a showroom near Jareeb Chowki and submitted documents, planning to pay the advance from the ransom money. Call records showed that Rachita called Prabhat 7-8 times within an hour after the murder. Prabhat had also taken Kushagra’s mobile phone, later recovered from the Tejab Mill campus. Gangster Act and police action All three accused were arrested and sent to jail. On March 31, 2024, police invoked the Gangster Act against them, declaring Prabhat Shukla as the gang leader. With the conviction now recorded, the court will announce the sentence on January 22, bringing the case closer to its conclusion. News is being updated continuously...

stories.title: 'RSS and BJP want to abolish constitution':Congress leader says, 'Modi wants to starve poor and divert country’s wealth to industrialists Ambani and Adani'
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that the BJP-led government is deliberately weakening welfare schemes to benefit industrialists like Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani on Tuesday. Speaking during his visit to his parliamentary constituency, Raebareli, Gandhi said PM Modi wants to centralise all power and “starve the poor” by dismantling social security mechanisms meant for workers and marginalised communities. ‘Mahatma Gandhi’s name removed, protection of the poor taken away’ Rahul Gandhi accused the Modi government of insulting Mahatma Gandhi by removing his name from the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) Act, 2005. However, he said the real issue was not the change of name, but the erosion of protections that the scheme provided to the poor. “The Modi government has destroyed the security that was given to the poor people of this country,” Gandhi said, adding that while Congress works to protect the public, the PM is diverting the country’s wealth into the hands of a few corporates. Congress launches nationwide movement to save MGNREGA The Congress leader said his party has launched a nationwide movement to save MGNREGA and stands firmly with labourers and workers. “Modi wants MGNREGA to end so that the money meant for sisters and workers goes directly to Ambani, Adani and other big industrialists,” Gandhi alleged. “Since they cannot do this openly, they are slowly strangling the Act.” ‘RSS-BJP want to destroy the constitution’ Rahul Gandhi further alleged that the RSS and the BJP want to abolish the Constitution and erase the ideologies of Dr B.R. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi. “They want to take India back to a time before Independence, where people’s land could be snatched, their rights taken away, and they pushed towards starvation,” he said, urging people to unite against such forces. Raebareli visit and public engagements Rahul Gandhi arrived in Raebareli late on Monday night. On Tuesday morning, he met Congress and Samajwadi Party workers and inaugurated the Raebareli Premier League T-20 cricket tournament. He interacted with players and even tossed a coin for the match. Later, he held a village meeting (chaupal) and interacted with MGNREGA workers to hear their concerns. Sixth visit after 2024 elections This was Rahul Gandhi’s sixth visit to Raebareli since the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. He had earlier visited the constituency on September 10, 2025. Concluding his remarks, Gandhi said, “The government of India today belongs to Ambani and Adani, not to farmers and labourers. Such a government will only cause immense harm to the country.”

stories.title: Nine-year-old found hanging inside closed college in Kanpur:Grandmother missing, police probe suicide or murder; await autopsy report
stories.summary: The body of a nine-year-old girl was found hanging inside a classroom at Baba Baijnath Degree College, a closed institution owned by Cabinet Minister Rakesh Sachan, police said on Tuesday. The college has remained shut since 2016. Body found hanging, TV on in room The child was found hanging from a ceiling fan with a dupatta, while a television was switched on inside the room. The incident came to light after the night watchman spotted the body and informed the police. A forensic team later reached the spot and collected evidence. Girl lived on college premises with grandmother The girl, identified as Vaishnavi alias Rani, was living on the college premises with her maternal grandmother (nani), who has been missing since the incident. Vaishnavi was a Class 2 student at a primary school. Police said they were surprised to find that her school identity card listed her maternal grandfather (nana) as her father and her maternal grandmother as her mother. Probe underway, stepfather questioned by police Investigators said the case is being examined from both murder and suicide angles. The girl’s stepfather, Manjeet, a resident of Babupurwa, was questioned by the police. Manjeet said his wife Laxmi had Vaishnavi from her first marriage and that the child was being cared for by her grandmother Mamta. He said he and Laxmi have two daughters together, Riddhi and Kirti, and the family lives in Babupurwa, while Vaishnavi stayed with her grandmother at the closed college near Barnav Mod in Ghatampur. Grandmother missing, phone switched off Manjeet said Vaishnavi studied at a primary school in Kripalpur and had not expressed any distress when the family met her during Raksha Bandhan. He said the watchman called late on Monday night to inform them that the girl had been found hanging, after which he and his wife rushed to the college. Since then, Mamta has been untraceable, and her mobile phone remains switched off. The matter has been reported to the police. Police said the television was on in the room and a chair was found lying away from the bed. Watchman recounts discovery The night watchman, Kamta, a resident of Dharamangadhpur village under Ghatampur police station limits, told police that Mamta would usually come every night to check whether the college gate was locked. However, she did not appear on Monday night. During his patrol, Kamta noticed the room door open. After receiving no response to his calls, he went inside and found the child hanging from the ceiling fan. ACP Krishnakant Yadav said- The case is being investigated with seriousness. The forensic team has gathered necessary evidence. Further action will be taken after receiving the post-mortem report. Police are also searching for the grandmother. Police await post-mortem report; college hosted training camp last year ACP Krishnakant Yadav said the case was being investigated thoroughly and that the forensic team had collected all necessary evidence. “Further action will be taken after the post-mortem report. Efforts are also underway to trace the grandmother,” he said, adding that police have questioned both the watchman and the child’s stepfather. Police also said that about a year ago, a village industry training camp was organised at the college by a foundation run by the minister’s daughter, Rashi Sachan. The month-long programme trained women and young girls from nearby villages in skills such as beautician work, tailoring and box-making. No activities have been held at the college since then.

stories.title: Purnea MP Pappu Yadav calls Dhirendra Shastri ‘thief’ ‘swindler’:Questions his public statements on nationalism, caste and religion; asks people to refrain from following ‘fraudulent’ ways
stories.summary: Purnea MP Pappu Yadav has called Madhya Pradesh's Bageshwar Dham's Peethadheeshwar Dhirendra Shastri a thief and swindler. Speaking to the media, Yadav said, 'Who is this Dhirendra Shastri?' When journalists said he is a religious preacher, Pappu Yadav said, 'You are making a thief and swindler into a preacher, is he Osho, is he Acharya Ramamurti?' Actually, at Patna airport, when a journalist asked him about Dhirendra Shastri's recent statement (if the moon comes on Tricolour, the country will not remain safe), the MP got angry. Further said, 'That one Baba of ours who is very lovely, who always keeps smiling, Premanand Baba. Respect such Babas. This thief-swindler, who has nothing to do with Sanatan, knows nothing about Sanatan; you talk about him.' Taunt on Vrindavan's storyteller Indresh Upadhyay Purnea MP also targeted Vrindavan's famous religious preacher Indresh Upadhyay, along with Dhirendra Shastri. On December 5, religious preacher Indresh Upadhyay married Shipra Sharma from Haryana in Jaipur, Rajasthan. A lot of money was spent on this wedding. 500 VIPs, including Pandit Dhirendra Shastri and poet Kumar Vishwas, attended this. Regarding this, Pappu Yadav said, 'There is a Baba worth Rs 300 crores, who just got married in Rajasthan. Let India follow Krishna's path, let it follow Guru Nanak's path, let it follow Buddha's path, let it become Ambedkarite. Why are you people making India follow these fraudulent ways?' The wedding Mandap was built in the style of Tirupati Balaji Temple Religious preacher Indresh Upadhyay got married in Jaipur. Where 101 priests from Haridwar, Nasik, and Vrindavan performed the wedding rituals and ceremonies according to Vedic traditions. The main wedding ceremonies lasted for about 3 hours. Storyteller Devi Chitralekha attended with her husband at the wedding mandap built in the style of Tirupati Balaji Temple. Additionally, Sadhvi Ritambhara, Acharya Punderik Goswami, Sanjeev Krishna Shastri, and Mahant Raju Das of Ayodhya Hanumangarhi, along with many saints and celebrities, attended this wedding. Now know that statement of Pandit Dhirendra Shastri, over which question MPs got angry Let us tell you that recently, RSS's centenary Hindu conference was held in Banda, UP. Where Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri had said, 'The day the moon comes in the tricolour, neither Sharma will survive, nor Verma will survive, neither Kshatriya will survive, nor Ravidas followers will survive, nor will Tulsidas followers survive, meaning no Hindu will survive.' Bageshwar Dham Sarkar also said that 'Today the country needs nationalism, not casteism. Dhirendra Shastri further said that if Hindus remain divided into castes, society will have to bear its loss.' Know what MP Pappu Yadav has previously said about Dhirendra Shastri MP has also called Dhirendra Shastri a ruffian MP Pappu Yadav has previously attacked storyteller Pandit Dhirendra Shastri. In a YouTube channel podcast, Pappu Yadav referred to Dhirendra Shastri as a 'ruffian' while mentioning his name. He said that today, many such people have emerged in society who are misleading people by using religious platforms. 'Such Babas should drown themselves' During the Kumbh Mela in Uttar Pradesh, religious preacher Pandit Dhirendra Shastri's statement after the death of several devotees in a stampede incident created a major controversy. After the accident, Dhirendra Shastri had said that dying at Kumbh leads to salvation. His statement faced anger from opposition parties and social organisations. Pappu Yadav had strongly protested against this statement in Parliament. Attacking Dhirendra Shastri, Pappu Yadav had said, 'Such Babas and people connected with money and politics should drown themselves.' He had said that the people who died in the stampede were poor and helpless, and it is inhuman to justify their deaths by calling it salvation.

stories.title: AAP protests in Lucknow over temple demolition in Kashi:Police detain leaders, drag workers into buses, and take them to Eco Garden after heated clash protest
stories.summary: Aam Aadmi Party held a strong protest in Lucknow against the demolition of ancient temples at Manikarnika Ghat in Kashi. They had a heated argument with the police. Police dragged and carried AAP leaders and workers to put them in buses. They were taken to Eco Garden. Party's District General Secretary Gyan Singh Kushwaha said that this government wants to erase our history. The government is destroying old temples. It is directly attacking our culture. This government is building its new empire. This is a completely anti-Hindu government. See 3 pictures of the protest... Protest held on state in-charge's direction District officials conducted this protest at the direction of the party's state in-charge MP Sanjay Singh. AAP says this matter is not just about construction or development, but is connected to faith, tradition, and respect for cultural heritage. The party alleged that tampering with religious sites in the name of development is not acceptable, and accountability will be fixed for those responsible. Demand for fixing accountability Party leaders said that Manikarnika Ghat is an important symbol of Kashi's identity and Sanatan tradition. Any kind of demolition of ancient temples here has hurt people's religious sentiments. AAP has demanded an impartial investigation of the entire matter and strict action against the culprits from the administration.
