stories.title: 1971 war hero Ram Ugrah Singh’s bravery remembered:Indian Army lance naik destroyed 3 enemy bunkers in East Pakistan, honored with Maha Vir Chakra
stories.summary: November 1971, East Pakistan, which is today's Bangladesh. Pakistan was oppressing its own Bengali citizens. Villages were being burned, and people were being killed. Millions of Bengali-speaking Pakistanis were entering India's Bengal and Assam to save their lives. 8 million people were standing at India's border seeking refuge. This wasn't just a refugee crisis, but a sign of impending war. The question wasn't whether there would be a fight, but when it would happen. Across the border, the Pakistani army was fully prepared, while India was still in preparation. Under these circumstances, 20 Mountain Division was given an important responsibility. Usually stationed in high-altitude mountainous areas along the border, it was tasked with capturing the Bogura post of East Pakistan as part of a special strategy. In this division, Lance Naik Ram Ugrah Pandey was commanding a small section (the smallest unit of the army). In the coming days, this name was going to make history while fighting on the difficult and swampy terrain of 'Morapara'. The story begins on November 20, 1971... Before that, let's get to know some officers of the 20 Mountain Division. These are the characters who were about to write history. A division is divided into several units, like a Brigade, Company, Platoon, etc. Similarly, Brigadier Farhat Bhatti was the Commanding Officer of 202 Mountain Brigade. Its most important battalion, 8 Guards Infantry, was commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Shamsher Singh, and in this same 8 Guards' D Company, one section was under Lance Naik Ram Ugrah Singh's charge. Let's now begin the story... November 20, 1971 Brigadier Farhat Bhatti called Lieutenant Colonel Shamsher Singh to the command headquarters. As soon as Lt. Col. Singh entered the Brigadier's cabin, he saluted and, standing tall, said- "Jai Hind..." Brigadier Bhatti asked- "How are the preparations...?" Lt. Col. Singh replied, "The soldiers are ready to die and kill for the country." Brigadier Bhatti immediately said, "Keep this spirit alive. But don't die for the country, just kill. I don't want any of my soldiers to become martyrs." Lt. Colonel Singh smiled, nodded in agreement, and said - "It will be done, sir..." Brigadier Bhatti - "The Pakistanis are strong. We haven't received attack orders yet. Pakistan might attack first. The unit must stay alert." Lt. Colonel Singh - "The unit is ready, sir." After this meeting, Lt. Colonel Shamsher Singh went to meet with the battalion soldiers. Ram Ugrah from 'D Company' was also present there. Lt. Colonel Singh told them about his conversation with the Brigadier, saying - "We have to capture the Bogura post. For this, we'll need to take control of Hili town. There are fields and swamps on the enemy's side; there will be many difficulties." Then, suddenly speaking with enthusiasm - "Will we overcome this challenge?" All soldiers replied in unison - "There's no doubt about it, sir. We will fight, we will win." Hili was a town between India and East Pakistan. The Indian side had settlements and roads, while the Pakistani side had paddy fields, muddy plains, and small villages like Morpara, Basudevpur, and Chandipur. Evening of November 22. There was tension at the border. War could break out anytime. The Indian army was ready. The plan was clear: capture Bogura, so that the Pakistani army could be isolated in North-East Pakistan. The most direct route went through Hili. For this, they first had to capture Morpara village. Lt. Colonel Singh was explaining the plan to his companions. He said, "The Pakistani Army's 205 Infantry Brigade has strong preparations here. Are you aware of this?" A soldier replied enthusiastically- "Yes, sir." Lt. Colonel asked- "What do you know?" No one spoke. Then, Section Commander Ram Ugrah Pandey said, "Sir, whatever preparations the enemies have made. We will foil their plans." Lt. Colonel Singh wanted to see the enthusiasm of the soldiers. He said, "The time is approaching. This is a chance to repay the debt of the country's salt. I want to tell you all something." He began to explain further- "The enemies have built solid concrete bunkers. They have converted old railway bogies into firing positions. They have installed barbed wire in multiple layers. Mines have been laid. Machine guns, recoilless rifles, and tanks are deployed." He spread out a map. The village of Morpara was marked with a red sign. Lt. Colonel Singh said in a serious voice- "Soldiers, Morpara is the enemy's strongest post. Artillery will attack first, then we will advance. The darkness of night will help us." The soldiers' enthusiasm was at its peak. Just then, Lance Naik Ram Ugrah Pandey's voice came from behind- "Bravery is our identity. This time, this identity will become even stronger, sir." The plan meeting ended. Shamsher Singh left, but Ram Ugrah stayed there with his companions. He gathered the soldiers of his section. Fire was burning in everyone's eyes. Ram Ugrah said with full force, "The enemy is strong. The firing will also be intense, but we are Guards. We will crawl forward, use grenades, and cover each other. No one will stay behind." Some soldiers hesitated at the mention of war. Someone said, "There is a swamp on the other side. What if we get stuck?" Ram Ugrah said with a slight smile but stern voice - "I will be in front, I will make the way. Even if I fall, don't stop. You people, keep moving forward." November 23, around 12 at night. 10 days before the declaration of war on December 3 Indian Artillery started firing to capture Hilli. The ground shook with the thundering of cannons. Shells began falling on Pakistani bunkers. Retaliatory attacks also began from their side. Fire and smoke had spread everywhere, but the enemy bunkers were still standing. India's plan did not go as expected, and the army suffered significant losses. At 1 AM, the attack was intensified. Two companies of 8 Guards moved forward. Lance Naik Ram Ugrah Pandey's section unit was crawling forward. Indian soldiers were standing in front of the enemy's strongest security line. The first obstacle was barbed wire. Beyond the wire were enemy bunkers. Ram Ugrah Pandey took out wire cutters, then looked around. All soldiers were lying on the ground. Ram Ugrah cut all the wires one by one and made a path for the soldiers to move through. Fellow soldiers moved forward, but Ram Ugrah Pandey was at the front. Ram Ugrah whispered, "Be careful. There could be mines here." The soldiers were still crawling forward, but the Pakistani army was also alert. They suddenly started firing with machine guns. Bullets started whizzing over their heads. Ram Ugrah shouted - "Take cover immediately..." All soldiers were pressed against the ground. Breathing was heavy, but fingers were firmly fixed on triggers. No one backed down. The enemy's first bunker was in sight. It was clearly visible where the shower of bullets was coming from. The entire team was stuck there. Moving forward had become difficult. Ram Ugrah made a decision based on the situation. He took out a grenade from his pouch and commanded sternly, "Give me covering fire. I'll do something." Fellow soldiers started firing their rifles towards the bunker. Bullets were falling on the bunker like streaks of lightning. Ram Ugrah was moving forward under the cover fire. His body was covered in mud. Even crawling required full strength. Sometimes feet would sink in the swamp, sometimes hands would slip in the mud. Nothing was clearly visible in the darkness, but the Lance Naik didn't stop. The bunker was still about ten meters away. The voices of Pakistani soldiers could be clearly heard from inside the bunker. The Pakistani firing machine gun bursts shouted in anger and panic - "These Indians have come so close. Look, they're crawling in the mud like worms...! Fire fully, kill these infidels; no one should survive." Then another Pakistani soldier said, "Sir, the magazine is empty. Artillery won't help. What should we do, retreat...?" The Pakistani section officer growled, "Shut up, our bunker is strong. Even if they come crawling, our machine gun will tear them apart. Just keep an eye on the tracer rounds. When they come closer, give them a full burst. No infidel will survive, Allah is with us." Just then, the rifleman shouted- "Allah... that Indian is going to throw a grenade. Fire in that direction, that direction...!" Before they could do anything, Lance Naik Ram Ugrah threw the grenade. His breathing intensified. For a moment, he was afraid whether the grenade would land in the right place or not. But in the next moment, the grenade spinning through the air landed right at the mouth of the bunker. There was a loud explosion. A cloud of smoke rose from the bunker, and the firing stopped. A soldier providing cover fire to Ram Ugrah said, "Sir, the bunker has collapsed." The soldiers were filled with enthusiasm. India had broken through East Pakistan's first line of defense. Everyone felt the path was opening up, but Lance Naik Ram Ugrah had severe pain in his shoulder. Actually, several grenade splinters had also penetrated his body. A splinter had also hit his face. The pain was so intense that it could take your breath away for a moment, yet he gritted his teeth and composed himself. He didn't tell his fellow soldiers anything. Just then, a soldier approached him - "Oh, what's this, sir... are you alright?" Lance Naik Ram Ugrah said enthusiastically - "Don't I look fine to you?" The soldier said, "Sir, please stop." The Lance Naik scolded him, saying, "This is not the time to stop. You people go this way. Stop the Pakistani firing there so that the second section can advance. I'll take care of those two bunkers. The face is damaged, but not the spirit." Other comrades came to know about the Lance Naik being wounded. Another soldier grabbed Ram Ugrah's hand and said- "Sir, look at your condition... your body is covered in blood. You go to the unit, I'll handle the section." Ram replied in a stern voice- "No... this is my section. Only cowards retreat." Another soldier stepped forward and said, "Sir, you are wounded. If you fall, we will all break down. At least go back to the medical point. We will stay here and provide cover. The rear battalion will handle everything else." Lance Naik Ram Ugrah took a deep breath. His face contorted with pain, but there was passion in his eyes. He looked at the first soldier and said- "Listen, if I retreat now, this battle will be suspended. The enemy will think we have weakened. We have advanced so far that going back is not possible. We will either move forward or only our dead bodies will go back." Just then, heavy firing came from another Pakistani bunker. The bullet went straight into a soldier's chest. There was a 'thud' sound, and he immediately collapsed. His eyes remained open. The sudden gunfire startled the entire team. Lance Naik Ram Ugram went to the screaming soldier. Through gritted teeth, he said, ''Pakistanis... move forward, no one should escape. Open heavy fire." Hearing this, the blood of the entire unit boiled. The soldiers gripped their rifles tightly. One soldier said, "Sir, now watch, we won't spare them. I'll either die or kill them all." At that moment, voices of Pakistani soldiers came from the other bunker - "He's dead. Now we'll send all Indian dogs to hell." Their abuses and slogans were echoing in the air. Hearing this, Ram Ugrah boiled with anger. Even while wounded, he was moving forward. Some enemy bullets were passing over his head. Ram Ugrah saw the right opportunity; the target was close. He threw a grenade to the left side of the bunker. In the darkness of night, Pakistani soldiers thought Indian soldiers were on that side. They turned their firing to the left. Seeing the opportunity, Ram Ugrah threw another grenade. Flames rose up, and smoke spread everywhere. The Lance Naik turned back to look at the team. Speaking with twice the enthusiasm in his voice, he said, "The second one is gone too..." Now it was time to blow up the third bunker. Being at a higher elevation made it quite dangerous. Without destroying it, Hilli could not be captured. Ram Ugrah made a new plan in just a few minutes. Then told his companions, "Four soldiers will attack from four directions." Then he told everyone their positions and started moving towards the third bunker. The bunker was visible. The machine gun barrel was gleaming with emerging bullets. Just then, a soldier said- "Sir, we're running out of cartridges and grenades." One soldier's gun had already stopped working. However, they had climbed so high that turning back was equivalent to death. An enemy bullet could pierce their chest at any moment. Lance Naik Ram Ugrah gave his gun to another companion. Now he only had hand grenades. He started moving forward with just that. At some distance, he spotted the body of a Pakistani soldier. In his enthusiasm, he had come quite far from the bunker and was killed in Indian firing. A rocket launcher lay beside him. Ram Ugrah said happily to himself, "Now we will strike them with their own weapons." He picked up both weapons and moved forward quickly. Blood was still flowing heavily from his wounded body, but he was at the front of the battle line. On the other side, bullets were raining heavily from the Pakistani bunker. Wherever the enemies sensed Indian presence, they would throw bombs. Indian soldiers could not advance without stopping the firing from that bunker. Lance Naik Ram Ugrah took a position with the rocket launcher at one spot. He set the target and pulled the trigger. With a loud explosion, the third bunker was also destroyed. At that exact moment, a bullet hit Ram Ugrah's chest, and he fell down there. Fellow soldiers ran to him. Blood was flowing rapidly. Ram Ugrah gathered his final strength. He looked towards his comrades and said in a breaking voice - "Don't stop, move forward... we have to win this war." And then suddenly his eyes closed. Lance Naik Ram Ugrah Pandey had been martyred. His team moved forward. The Pakistani army could only hold that front for one more day. The 8 Guards Infantry had completed their mission. Pakistan was split into two parts, laying the foundation of Bangladesh, and Ram Ugrah's martyrdom became immortal forever. The Government of India honored him with the Maha Vir Chakra posthumously in 1972 for his bravery. After receiving that honor from President VV Giri, his wife said- "They often used to say nothing is bigger than duty, and the country is bigger than family. They fulfilled their duty. There is pain in their absence, but there is also pride that what they used to say, they did exactly that." *** Story Edit - Krishna Gopal Graphics - Saurabh Kumar *** Creative liberty has been taken to make the story interesting.

stories.title: Brutal murder of event manager in Bareilly:Friend buries body in field; victim missing for 10 days; CCTV exposes truth
stories.summary: A 30-year-old event manager has been murdered in Bareilly. Police have arrested her friend on murder charges. According to police, the friend first drugged the event manager and then strangled her to death with a muffler. To avoid suspicion, the body was buried in a field. Police recovered Pooja's body from a field behind KCMT College. The incident took place in the Durga Nagar area of Baradari. The young woman has been identified as Pooja Rana. Family members had filed a missing person report on January 13. When police interrogated her friend Vimal based on suspicion, he confessed to the murder. The motive for murder has not yet been revealed. Police are also investigating the case from the angle of a love affair. Pooja Rana (30), an event manager living in Durga Nagar, left home on January 12, telling her mother and sister she was going for event. When she didn't return late at night, and her mobile phone started showing switched off, the family's concern grew. Family members called and asked Pooja's close friend, Vimal. Vimal said on the phone that he had dropped Pooja near her home. He asked if she hadn't reached home yet. Father Prem Singh said - After hearing about Pooja's disappearance, Vimal himself came to the house. When her mobile was switched off, they started searching but found no clues. After this, we filed a missing person report with the police. Then the police started examining CCTV footage. When the search for Pooja reached CCTV cameras, this conspiracy was exposed layer by layer. Vimal, whom Pooja's family considered close and with whom Pooja had a 'family-like relationship', was the one who murdered her. The accused Vimal, not only took Pooja's life, but also buried the body in a deserted field behind KCMT College in the Izzat Nagar police station area to destroy evidence. CCTV footage revealed the scene of death Police scanned CCTV footage of the area. Pooja was last seen with Vimal. After being taken into custody, Vimal initially misled the police, but broke down during intense interrogation. He confessed to his crime. Late Thursday night, the police team excavated the field based on the accused's identification and recovered the decomposed body. Timeline of the incident: From disappearance to recovery January 12 (Afternoon): Left home, saying she was going to a puja event. January 12 (12:00 AM): Accused Vimal misled the family by saying he had dropped Pooja near her home. January 13: When the mobile was switched off, father Prem Singh started searching, but found no clues. January 14-21: On the family's complaint, the police registered a missing case and started scanning CCTV footage. January 21 (Evening): Based on CCTV, Vimal was taken into custody and confessed to murder during interrogation. January 22 (Late Night): Police recovered Pooja's body from a field behind KCMT College. January 23: Post-mortem of the body is being conducted. Mother says - She left home smiling on the 12th At the district hospital morgue, Pooja's brother Manoj and mother Mahendra Devi are inconsolable. Pooja, third among four siblings, was very active in her work. Mother still can't believe that the daughter who left for work smiling on the 12th will never return. Family members say that Vimal used to frequently visit their house, so no one suspected him. Meanwhile, police have completed the panchnama of the body and sent it for post-mortem, and the accused is being interrogated. Pooja supported 50 families Girls who worked with Pooja say that their households ran because of Pooja didi. She supported at least 50 families. Pooja used to work at wedding party events and would send girls wherever they were needed for events. We only want the accused to be hanged. A girl said that when Pooja disappeared on the 12th, her status stated that she was going to Mumbai, and then that status was removed. This was Vimal's conspiracy. She was very caring, always thought about everyone. Vimal killed her in this way. He should meet the same fate. We demand that he be hanged. We want justice. Love affair could be the reason behind murder Between the initial police investigation and family allegations, monetary transactions are being cited as the reason for the murder. The victim's brother, Manoj Rana, alleges that after kidnapping Pooja, she was given some intoxicating substance and then strangled to death with a muffler. The brother also said that the sister had a scooter, three gold rings, two chains, and earrings. Vimal murdered her by strangling her with a muffler with the intention of looting these. However, police say the case may also be linked to a love affair. We are also closely investigating this aspect to determine whether Vimal carried out this incident alone or if someone else was also involved.

stories.title: CJM changed twice in 48 hours in Sambhal:Aditya Singh transferred, replacing judge who ordered FIR against ASP Chaudhary
stories.summary: A new Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) has been appointed for the second time in 48 hours in UP's Sambhal. Now, Kaushambi's CJM Deepak Kumar Jaiswal has been made the new CJM of Sambhal. Meanwhile, Sambhal CJM Aditya Singh has been sent back as Civil Judge (Senior Division), Chandausi. Additionally, Naved Akhtar has been appointed as Additional Senior Division Civil Judge, Chandausi, from Junior Division Judge, Sambhal. Aditya Singh was promoted just two days ago. He was made CJM Sambhal in place of Vibhanshu Sudhir, but lawyers were quite unhappy with this decision. It was Aditya Singh who had ordered the survey on the Shri Harihar Temple versus Shahi Jama Masjid claim in Sambhal. Vibhanshu was sent to Sultanpur as a Civil Judge, Senior Division. Let us tell you that the Allahabad High Court made a major reshuffle on Tuesday evening by transferring 14 judges. The shocking name in the list was Vibhanshu Sudhir. Vibhanshu had ordered the filing of an FIR against 20 policemen, including ASP Anuj Chaudhary, on January 9. It is alleged that during the Sambhal violence, ASP Anuj Chaudhary and other policemen shot a young man. Lawyers angered by judge's transfer, protested saying - murder of justice Where was Vibhanshu deployed? Now, let's understand why FIR orders were issued against the police personnel? In Sambhal's Nakhasa police station area, Yameen, who lives in Mohalla Khaggu Sarai Anjuman, filed a petition in the CJM court on February 6, 2025. Yameen had stated that his son, Alam, left home on November 24, 2024, to sell rusk (toast). When he reached the Shahi Jama Masjid area, the police shot him. Yameen had named 12 policemen, including the then CO Sambhal Anuj Chaudhary and Sambhal Kotwali Inspector Anuj Tomar, as accused. The case was heard in court on January 9, 2026. The Chief Judicial Magistrate had ordered an FIR to be registered against all police officers. Yameen's lawyer, Chaudhary Akhtar Hussain, said that his client's son got treatment while hiding from the police. The court was requested to file an FIR against former CO Anuj Chaudhary, former Inspector Anuj Tomar, and unknown police personnel. SP had said - Will appeal against the decision SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi had said - Judicial inquiry into the violence has been completed. Therefore, this FIR will not be registered. We will appeal against the court's decision. 4 died in violence during survey on November 24, 2024 The Hindu side had claimed that Sambhal's Jama Masjid was previously the Harihar Temple. Babur had it demolished in 1529 and built a mosque. A petition was filed in the Sambhal court regarding this on November 19, 2024. On the same day, Civil Judge Senior Division Aditya Singh ordered a survey inside the mosque. The court had appointed Ramesh Singh Raghav as Advocate Commissioner. That same day at 4 PM, the team reached the mosque for the survey. The survey was conducted for 2 hours. However, the survey was not completed that day. After this, on November 24, the survey team reached Jama Masjid. The survey was being conducted inside the mosque. During this time, a large number of people gathered. The crowd threw stones at the police team. After this, violence erupted. Four people died from gunshot wounds. SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi, prominent CO Anuj Chaudhary, Deputy Collector, along with 29 policemen, were injured. 3 women among 79 rioters were arrested After the violence, police arrested 79 rioters, including 3 women. A total of 12 FIRs were registered at Sambhal Kotwali and Thana Nakhasa. FIR was registered against 40 people, including SP MP Ziaur Rahman Barq, SP MLA Iqbal Mahmood's son Suhail Iqbal and 2750 unknown people. On June 18, SIT filed a chargesheet of 1128 pages in court against 23 people, including MP Barq. However, SP MLA's son Suhail Iqbal's name is not included in the chargesheet. CJM Vibhanshu issued several orders against police personnel On December 24, 2025, CJM Vibhanshu Sudhir ordered an FIR against 13 police personnel, including then Inspector Pankaj Lawania, in the fake encounter case in Sambhal. These included 2 inspectors, 4 sub-inspectors and constables who were posted at the time of the incident. The court directed the Station House Officer of Bahajoi to register a case immediately and submit a report to court within 3 days. In the Thana Bahajoi area on July 7, 2022, Omvir, Dhirendra and Avnesh were arrested during an encounter. In the case presented before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Omvir had accused then CO Gopal Singh of staging a fake encounter. The court ordered that he should not be included in this case.

stories.title: 2 crore cash, 62 kg silver found in Kanpur:Police get tired counting notes, had to call for machine; 5 arrested
stories.summary: Police found Rs 2 crore cash and 62 kg silver from a house in Kanpur. The situation became such that police officers were sweating while counting such a large amount. Police had to call in machines to count the notes. The counting of notes went on for about 4 hours. Police officers got tired of collecting the silver. Actually, the police raided a house late at night. An international betting and hawala network was being run from the house. Police have arrested 5 people from the gang. Nepalese currency was also recovered from them. Police are gathering information about other gang members by interrogating the accused. Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal reached the spot to investigate based on the information. The raid was conducted in the Dhankutti locality of Collectorganj. Had been receiving hawala complaints for many days ADCP Sumit Sudhakar Ramteke of the Special Operation Group said - For the past several days, complaints of hawala, betting business and illegal share trading were being received in the city. Based on this, a raid was conducted at the house of Ramakant Gupta, a resident of Dhankutti, around 9 pm on Thursday. The police surrounded the house from all sides and went inside. Inside the house, they found a stash of notes and a significant amount of silver. When the police interrogated the suspects, they couldn't give proper answers. Police removed money stored in cartons. These contained bundles of 500-rupee notes. There were 500-rupee notes worth 1.80 crores. The rest were bundles of 200 and 100 rupees. Due to such a large amount, police also brought machines to count the notes and weigh the silver. Pen drives, modems, computers, laptops, etc., were recovered from the accused. Police have taken into custody Rahul Jain from Kidwai Nagar, Shivam Tripathi, Sachin Gupta from Yashoda Nagar Gangaganj, Vanshraj, and one other person. All five were reported to be friends. In the preliminary investigation, the names of some people from Delhi, Aligarh, Varanasi, Indore, Mumbai, Noida, and Jaipur have come up. More information about them is being gathered. ADCP Sumit Sudhakar Ramteke said- The accused were involved in cricket betting, hawala business and illegal stock market trading. The accused have connections with gangster and international cricket bookie Ankush Agarwal. Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal said- The gang's connections lead directly to Delhi and Noida. Deals have been made with several influential people. The arrested accused have named some influential people. Information is being gathered.

stories.title: Shankaracharya praises Keshav Maurya as CM material:Avimukteshwaranand falls sick during protest, receives treatment in van for 5 hours
stories.summary: Jyotish Peeth Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, who has been staging a sit-in protest outside his camp at the Prayagraj Magh Mela for five days, on Friday praised Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya as a “wise leader” and said he should be made the Chief Minister. The Shankaracharya claimed that Maurya understands the mistakes made by officials and that the issue should not be allowed to escalate. “He knows that our officials erred, and he believes this matter should not have been blown out of proportion. This dispute is harming us. A sensible leader like him should become the Chief Minister. Someone driven by ego and stubbornness should not hold the post,” the Shankaracharya said. Deputy CM’s statement and the ongoing row The Shankaracharya’s remarks came amid a dispute between him and the Magh Mela administration. On Thursday, Deputy CM Keshav Maurya had said he bowed to the Shankaracharya’s feet and requested him to take the holy dip. He also assured that if any saint or Shankaracharya was insulted, an inquiry would be conducted and strict action would be taken. However, Swami Avimukteshwaranand has been demanding an apology from the administration and has refused to take a holy bath until his demand is met. He has also alleged that administrative officials are playing a “notice-notice” game. Health deteriorates during protest On Friday morning, the Shankaracharya’s health deteriorated and he developed a high fever. From 10 am to 3 pm, he rested inside a vanity van after taking medication. Later, when a crowd gathered, he came out and sat on his palanquin. Despite his illness, he continued the protest. Due to the ongoing dispute, he did not take the holy dip at the Sangam on Basant Panchami, which is considered an important ritual during the Magh Mela. Administrative standoff and past remarks Earlier, speaking to Bhaskar, Swami Avimukteshwaranand had said, “Until the administration apologizes, I will not bathe. I have not yet taken the Mauni Amavasya bath, so how can I take the Basant Panchami bath?” He claimed that the administration has remained silent after issuing two notices. Meanwhile, Puri Peeth Shankaracharya Swami Nishchalanand Saraswati took a holy dip at the Triveni Sangam on Basant Panchami, reaching the riverbank in a wheelchair. Swami Avimukteshwaranand had brought around 1.25 lakh clay Shivlings to the Magh Mela for installation. However, following the controversy on Mauni Amavasya, he could not install them. Earlier, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, without naming anyone, had warned that no one has the right to disrupt tradition and cautioned against those who, under the guise of religion, try to weaken Sanatan Dharma. Deputy CM Keshav Maurya reiterated his appeal, urging the Shankaracharya to take a holy dip and resolve the issue. To know the latest update, go through the live blog…

stories.title: Saint community divided over Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand dispute:Urges ending politics, condemns violence, insists apology from administration
stories.summary: The saint community is divided over the Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand dispute in Prayagraj. Some support him, while others oppose. Aniruddhacharya Maharaj criticized the administration for allegedly assaulting sadhus, while Ravindra Puri said anyone abusing the CM cannot be a saint. Shankaracharya Sadanand Saraswati said - Batuk Brahmins were beaten, this is wrong Shankaracharya Sadanand Saraswati of Dwarka's Sharda Peeth says that the administration does not understand the meaning of Shikha, by grabbing which they beat the saints. The Shikha is where Brahma resides. It is wrong that Shankaracharya and Batuk Brahmins were beaten for taking a bath in the Ganges. This is the arrogance of governance. One should never misuse their power. Those who prevent bathing in the Ganges incur the sin of cow slaughter. This is the word of scripture. Therefore, such acts should not be done. If we have been given any power, we should not misuse it. We strongly condemn this act of the administration. Aniruddhacharya said - Administration should apologize Storyteller Aniruddhacharya Maharaj said - The administration has made a mistake. They grabbed Brahmins and sadhus by their hair and beat them. Why isn't the administration apologizing? Why is there such a delay in apologizing? Saints are compassionate; they will forgive immediately. What is the administration's ego in asking for forgiveness? Who gave you the right to grab someone's hair and beat them? Did the Constitution give you this right? Go to the feet of saints, if a mistake was made, apologize. The administration should not drag this out. When one seeks refuge, saints forgive. Nischlanand called Avimukteshwaranand 'Favorite' Govardhan Math's Shankaracharya Swami Nischalanand Saraswati of Puri said - Avimukteshwaranand's decision is irrefutable. Even the Supreme Court recognizes his decisions. He showed affection towards Avimukteshwaranand by calling him his 'favorite'. Shankaracharya said - Any dispute can only be responded to when it is officially brought to their attention. This is like inviting a terrible war. Until our blood boils, all this will continue. Ravindra Puri said - A saint who calls CM son of Humayun is not a saint Mahant Ravindra Puri, President of Akhil Bharatiya Akhada Parishad, said - Mini Mahakumbh is going on in Prayagraj. Regarding calling the Chief Minister the son of Akbar and Humayun, he said that this cannot be the language of a saint. If he had any complaint, he should have complained to the Chief Minister or gone to court. Why is he directly targeting the Chief Minister? We, the saint community, strongly condemn this. Strict action should be taken against Avimukteshwaranand. If anyone is working to advance Sanatan, it is the Prime Minister, Chief Minister, and Home Minister who are doing it. Ravindra Puri said - When the Ram temple was being built in Ayodhya, you (Avimukteshwaranand) asked why the Ram temple was being built? Wherever work happens, they oppose it. We cannot hear such things against the Prime Minister and the Chief Minister. Chief Minister Yogi himself is a saint and a Peethadheeshwar. We will not tolerate such a conspiracy against him. Will talk to the saints of the council. Shringverpur Peethadheeshwar said - Shankaracharya should not do politics Shringverpur's Peethadheeshwar Jagadguru Ramanujacharya Shandilya Maharaj said - The administration should not have gotten saints killed; this is wrong. Also, Shankaracharya should not do politics. He said - Some political people also want to enter among saints, which is wrong. There is no need for politics among saints. Shandilya Maharaj's target was on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Congress state president Ajay Rai. Ramanujacharya said - Nothing is spoiled yet, should apologize Jagadguru Ramanujacharya said - What good has Rambhadracharya done? Holding a staff in hand, we do not worship broken idols. If a Brahmin's body is broken, worship does not happen. 4 Shankaracharyas, 13 Akhadas, and 5 Vaishnacharyas saints are worthy of worship and veneration. They should have been respected; the administration should have arranged for them to come by palanquin. They should have requested that Maharaj give up the palanquin. Come walk with us, we will ensure your safe bathing. Nothing is ruined yet; apologize and put an end to the dispute. Not just in Prayagraj, if there is a need for protest in Delhi, the saint community is ready to do it. Devaki Nandan Thakur - Violence against saints is not right In Agra, Devakinandan Thakur said - This is a time of moral dilemma for me. Both sides are our own. On one side, there is Shankaracharya, who is like God; on the other side, there are those people who were concerned about the large number of people who came for bathing. I will only say that such a situation should not be escalated. Forgetting mutual differences, every Sanatani should resolve issues with love by sitting together in one voice, not complicate them. The administration should also ensure that those who wear a tilak on their forehead, have a shikha on their head, and wear saffron robes should be treated with respect. Such beating is not right. Now about the saints of Mathura Mahant Ramdas said - Insulting Batuk Brahmins is condemnable Mahant Ramdas Maharaj says - Shankaracharya Maharaj's position is high; he is our Simhastha. Similarly, Yogi Maharaj is also in a high position. He takes care of the entire UP. However, the insult to Batuk Brahmins is very condemnable. They are servants of Sanatan. Why were they insulted? The administration must explain this. In our religion, fingers are easily pointed. Try pointing at Maulana Sahib, Haji Sahib in Islam. This position of Shankaracharya is Lord Shiva's position. This is a Brahmin who serves, practices celibacy, is a lord of earth, and has knowledge of the Vedas. They have their own beliefs. Shankaracharya's fast is not appropriate, but using batons on Brahmins is also wrong Mahant Atul Krishna Maharaj of Parikrama Marg in Vrindavan said - I just want to say that saints, mahants, and householders should not be divided. What is happening on the land of Prayagraj seems to be going towards a different kind of politics. The fast undertaken by Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was not appropriate. The police administration's use of batons on their Brahmins was also wrong. We request Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to completely end this tug of war. Words of Kashi's Saints Swami Chakrapani said - Young priests should be worshipped, not oppressed Swami Chakrapani Maharaj said - Kumbh and Magh Mela are not the contribution of any single person; they are the invaluable heritage of sages, seers, and saint tradition. Maintaining its dignity is the collective responsibility of the government, administration, and the saint community. He described the incident of fighting with the boys and pulling their hair as a condemnable and heinous crime. Said that the boys should be worshipped and served, not subjected to atrocities. The braid is a symbol of the Sanatan tradition. An attack on it is an attack on the dignity of Sanatan. He said that the people of Prayag and Kashi are known for sin-redemption, charity-virtue, and service to saints. Every wrong deed committed at such holy places cannot escape divine justice. He asked the administration to apologize to the saints and priests. Jitendranand said - Such evidence in court, cannot consider him Shankaracharya Swami Jitendranand Saraswati, National General Secretary of Akhil Bharatiya Sant Samiti, gave a strong statement. Said - There is such evidence present in court, based on which Avimukteshwaranand cannot be considered Shankaracharya. They get beaten every time, this time they were creating disorder during the bath. According to the document, until a final decision is made regarding the Shankaracharya position, neither Swami Avimukteshwaranand nor any other person can be appointed or enthroned as Shankaracharya. The order also states that providing any facilities to Avimukteshwaranand as Shankaracharya will be considered contempt of court. This matter is pending in the Supreme Court as a civil appeal. In 26 years, they have engaged in violence at the fair multiple times. Now the words of Ayodhya's saints Hanumangarhi's priest Tulsidas said - He is conspiring at the behest of Congress Acharya Pandit Rakesh Das of Ayodhya's Jyotish Bhavan said - Swami Avimukteshwaranand is a symbol of faith and respect. He was going for a Ganga bath, not by any vehicle but by palanquin. There were 100 people with him. Under these circumstances, stopping him from taking a Ganga bath was not appropriate in any way. Hanumangarhi's priest Tulsidas says - Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand is conspiring against the government at the behest of Congress. Mahant Ramkumar Das said - Swami Avimukteshwaranand's going for a Ganga bath while sitting on a palanquin should not be called appropriate at all. This is Kalpvas's Magh Mela, not Mahakumbh's bath. Such behavior is not appropriate in any way in the world. Senior Naga Shatrughna Das of Hanumangarhi's Ujjainia Patti said - Swami and Avimukteshwaranand lack knowledge; they should chant Sitaram Sitaram. Read what happened on Mauni Amavasya On January 18, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was going for a bath in a palanquin during Mauni Amavasya at the Magh Mela. The police stopped Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand's palanquin. Police asked him to walk to Sangam on foot. Shankaracharya's disciples did not agree and started moving forward with the palanquin. This led to pushing and shoving between the disciples and the police. Police took several disciples into custody. Police also beat up a sadhu at the police station. This angered Shankaracharya, and he insisted on getting his disciples released. Officers tried to reason with him, folded their hands, but he did not agree. After this, the police took several more supporters of Shankaracharya into custody. Shankaracharya's palanquin was pulled and taken 1 km away from the Sangam. During this, the palanquin's canopy also broke. Shankaracharya could not even take a bath.

stories.title: Businessman’s son kidnapped, murdered, body packed in box:Chitrakoot police kill accused in encounter; within 2 hours after ₹40 lakh ransom demand
stories.summary: In Chitrakoot, UP, police have encountered two accused who kidnapped and murdered a businessman's son. Police killed one accused in the encounter, while the other was shot in the leg. Both criminals had kidnapped businessman Ashok Kesarwani's 13-year-old son 24 hours ago. They had demanded ransom. When they didn't receive the ransom, both murdered the businessman's son late Thursday night. Police surrounded both criminals on Friday morning. As soon as they saw the police, both started firing. In retaliatory action, police killed a criminal named Kallu, while his accomplice Irfan was shot in the leg. See pictures... Now know the full case in 4 pointers.... Trader's son abducted in broad daylight, then ransom demanded: In the Bargad police station area, in broad daylight, miscreants abducted Ayush Kesarwani, son of trader Ashok Kesarwani, a resident of Bargad market. Shortly after the abduction, a ransom was demanded from the family. The police and family were engaged in negotiations and search, but when the ransom was not paid, the miscreants brutally murdered the child. Body found in a locked box, people stunned upon breaking the lock: During the search, the police found a locked box. When the lock of the box was broken, Ayush's body was recovered inside. The sight was so horrific that the people present at the scene were stunned. As soon as the news of the body's discovery spread, a sensation and outrage spread throughout the Bargad area. One kidnapper killed in police encounter: During police action in the kidnapping-murder case, one accused was killed in an encounter. The deceased accused has been identified as Kallu alias Sahve Iman (about 70 years old), resident of Katra Chauraha, Karma, Ghurpur police station. According to the police, he was killed by a bullet in the encounter. Identification of the second accused, continuous raids in search Police have apprehended the second accused involved in this heinous crime by shooting him in the leg. He has been identified as Irfan Ansari, son of Aftab Alam, resident of Katra Chauraha, Karma, Ghurpur Police Station. Security has been increased in the district regarding the entire matter and the investigation has been intensified. News is being updated....

stories.title: Birthday girl creates ruckus on Kanpur highway:Sits on car window while driving at 100 km/h; cuts 10 cakes placed on vehicle's bonnet
stories.summary: On Aligarh Highway in Kanpur, the birthday girl and her friends created a huge ruckus. The girl cut 10 cakes on the car's bonnet. Then set off fireworks on the highway. After that, she sat on the car window and drove at 100 kmph on the highway. Two cars kept following behind her. The incident happened on Tuesday at 12 midnight, its video surfaced on Thursday. In which two girls are seen celebrating a birthday on the highway with 6 boys. The birthday girl's name is Mayra Thakur. She is a resident of the Barra police station area. Earlier, on December 29, a video of Mayra had surfaced. In it, she was seen beating a young woman on the highway for her boyfriend. She had grabbed her hair and dragged her on the road. Girl said - It's 12 o'clock, see what we do A video surfaced on social media on Thursday. This video is from Kanpur Aligarh Highway. It was shared from a social media handle named Sakshi Mishra. In the video, a girl named Mayra Thakur is seen wearing a birthday belt. She is accompanied by her female friend. Her friend can be seen saying in the video, You know today is my sister's birthday. It's 12 o'clock at night, and we are going. Now see what we do? More than 6 youths in three cars, who were part of the girl's birthday celebration, parked their cars on the highway. Fireworks on highway after cutting cake One of these cars has about 10 cakes placed on the bonnet, which the birthday girl cuts. After cutting the cake, massive fireworks are set off on the highway railing. After this, everyone gets into all three cars. A girl can be seen sitting on the driver's side window in the leading car. While a young man is sitting in the left side window of the car, he is shooting her video. Both cars are racing at high speed on the highway from behind. Car passengers are making videos from behind. Mayra beat up a girl over boyfriend Another video of Mayra went viral on December 29, 2025. The video was from the Yashoda Nagar bypass. In it, Mayra and a girl were seen fighting over a boyfriend. Mayra slammed the other girl on the road. She grabbed her hair and dragged her on the road. Then she slapped her 11 times while pulling her hair. After that, she rained kicks and punches on her chest and head. During this time, Mayra's female companion kept making a video of the incident. Mayra was saying that you had left Abhishek. Now that he has become mine, you will call him babu. Tell me, will you call him Babu? While the other girl kept apologizing by holding her feet.

stories.title: Heavy rain hits western UP, Purvanchal sunny:Agra–Mathura among 7 districts soaked; hail alert in 18 districts as cold wave returns soon
stories.summary: Weather conditions across Uttar Pradesh have changed once again. Several districts in western UP witnessed spells of rain on Friday, while eastern parts of the state remained sunny. From late Thursday night, light to moderate rain accompanied by strong winds began in Noida, Ghaziabad and Meerut. During the day, rainfall was reported in Agra, Mathura, Meerut, Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Bulandshahr and several other districts. The sudden change in weather forced people indoors, roads appeared deserted, and those stepping out for essential work were seen carrying umbrellas and wearing raincoats. Hail alert issued The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a hailstorm alert for 18 districts, with the possibility of thunderstorms at isolated places. In contrast, eastern UP has remained largely unaffected so far. In Purvanchal, including Lucknow, Kanpur and nearby districts, the weather has stayed clear, with bright sunshine since morning. Cold wave likely to intensify again According to the India Meteorological Department, rain and snowfall have begun in the Himalayan states. As a result, cold winds moving southwards are expected to lower temperatures in eastern UP as well. The recent relief from cold and fog may be short-lived, as temperatures could drop by 3–4°C in the coming days. Fog is also likely to return in several districts. Lowest temperatures recorded Over the past 24 hours, Bahraich recorded the lowest night temperature at 6°C. It was followed by Gorakhpur (6.7°C), Barabanki and Ayodhya (7.0°C), and Azamgarh (7.2°C). Expert view Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said, The spell of rain has begun across the state. Rainfall may continue in several districts for the next two days. From January 25, the weather is likely to clear. Due to an active western disturbance over northern Pakistan, fluctuations in weather conditions will persist.

stories.title: Why do people keep 'shikha' in Sanatan Dharma?:From Vedic rituals and Chanakya’s vow to meditational energy beliefs
stories.summary: In Sanatan Dharma, many people keep a tuft of hair (shikha) on the head because the spot is traditionally linked with the Sahasrara Chakra. It is believed this area is connected to spiritual energy, and keeping a shikha helps keep it active, making meditation and concentration easier. As a result, followers feel it supports better control over the mind, intellect, and body, which is why the practice has continued. Chanakya's Shikha Pledge Question: What is the importance of keeping a choti (tuft of hair)? Answer: In Hinduism, there are 16 types of sacraments described from birth to the death of a person. Each has its own importance. One of these is the Mundan ceremony. The mundan (head-shaving ceremony) is performed in the first, third, or fifth year of a child. During this ritual, a small amount of the child's hair is left. The ritual of keeping shikha (tuft of hair) on the head is also performed during the Yajnopavit or Upanayana ceremony. According to Hindu beliefs, keeping a tuft of hair is necessary for performing worship, rituals, and yagnas. Maharaj Harichaitanya Brahmachari from Prayagraj explains - the place where the shikha is kept is traditionally considered a symbolic spot connected to the universe. It is believed that there is an interconnection between the shikha, navel, and heart. That's why the shikha is considered important. In many religious activities, while remembering or taking a sankalp (resolution), one first touches the shikha and pays respect. According to religious beliefs, every Hindu should keep a shikha. While it is considered especially necessary for Vedic Brahmins. However, detached Brahmins (who adopt the path of renunciation by separating from worldly life) sometimes do not keep a tuft of hair. Question: Since when has the tradition of keeping Choti (tuft of hair) been practiced in Sanatan Dharma? Answer: BHU Astrologer Prof. Vinay Pandey explains - The tradition of keeping Choti/Shikha in Sanatan Dharma is considered thousands of years old. According to historians and religious beliefs, this tradition has been continuing since the Vedic period. During that time, Gurukul education, Yagna, and Upanayan Sanskar held special importance. During that era, keeping a tuft of hair (choti) was considered a symbol of culture, discipline, and religious identity. Even today, many people adopt it by connecting it to their faith and tradition. Question: Is keeping a tuft of hair a religious rule or just tradition? Answer: In Sanatan Dharma, keeping a tuft of hair is not a strict religious rule. It is considered an ancient Vedic tradition and custom. According to religious beliefs, there has been a tradition of keeping shikha (tuft of hair) after the Upanayana ceremony. Especially among those who perform worship, yagya, and Vedic rituals. Question: How long should the shikha (tuft of hair) be? Answer: Vinay Pandey explains - According to religious beliefs, the shape of the Sahasrara chakra is considered similar to a cow's hoof (the lowest, hard, nail-like part of the foot). For this reason, many people keep their sikha (hair tuft) equal to the size of a cow's hoof. In astrology, it is said that if someone is experiencing negative effects of Rahu in their horoscope, keeping a sikha on the head is considered beneficial. This provides relief during Rahu's phase and starts bringing good results. Question: What is the scientific reason for keeping a sikha? Answer: Dr. Ashok Kumar Satpathy, Associate Professor in the Sanskrit Department of Lucknow University, explains - There is also a scientific reason behind keeping a sikha. The spot where the sikha is kept is the center of the brain. This location controls the body's organs, intellect, and mind. Keeping a choti (tuft of hair) keeps the Sahasrara chakra awakened. It helps in maintaining control over the intellect, mind, and body. The 7 chakras present in our body stay awakened. This maintains balance in our body. Where the choti is kept, there lies the Sushumna nadi, which provides positive energy to the body. The development of the entire body is considered to be related to the Sushumna nadi. Question: What are the rules for keeping a choti? Answer: According to Dr. Ashok Kumar Satpathy, there are rules for keeping a Choti (tuft of hair). While keeping a Choti, all hair from the head should be cut. The Choti should only be kept in the middle of the head. Religious scriptures describe the shape of the Choti to be similar to a cow's hoof. During charity, worship, and while eating, the Choti should be tied in a knot. Additionally, while performing daily activities, the Choti should be kept untied.

stories.title: Aggressive low bids put NHAI in a fix, trend may impact quality
stories.summary: Highway construction agencies are facing a challenge as contractors aggressively bid up to 48% below estimated project costs, raising concerns about work quality. This trend, driven by fewer projects and increased competition, forces contractors to quote low to keep resources engaged, potentially impacting the sector's long-term health and project standards.

stories.title: Congress says Modi government not serious about caste count in Census 2027
stories.summary: Congress has questioned the Modi government's intent regarding the caste enumeration in Census 2027, citing that the 'houselisting' questionnaire omits 'OBC' as an option. The party demands immediate consultations with political parties, states, and civil society before finalizing the caste census details.

stories.title: ‘Big armada’ near Iran: Trump says Tehran 'wants to talk, strike deal' amid rising tensions
stories.summary: President Trump announced a "big armada" is deployed near Iran, stating the situation remains in flux. While close to ordering strikes earlier this month, he delayed the decision, believing Tehran genuinely seeks a deal. The US has bolstered its military presence in the region, including an aircraft carrier strike group, as diplomatic options are also being considered.

stories.title: Congress brass may meet Shashi Tharoor to settle issues
stories.summary: Congress leadership is planning to meet senior leader Shashi Tharoor following his absence from a crucial Kerala election strategy meeting. Tharoor, who cited personal issues and unhappiness with the party, will be invited for discussions to address his grievances. The party aims to ensure unity for the upcoming state elections, recognizing Tharoor's electoral influence.

stories.title: Jessica Daugirdas dies at 35 after sharing her three-year colorectal cancer fight with followers
stories.summary: Jessica Daugirdas, a Brazilian influencer, died at 35 after a three-year fight with colorectal cancer. Her family confirmed her death on Instagram on January 25. Known for sharing her health journey online, Jessica inspired thousands with her honesty, strength, and faith while facing cancer and its many challenges.

stories.title: Use gender-neutral terms, courts told
stories.summary: Delhi High Court has adopted gender-neutral terminology in court documents, replacing father's/husband's name with parent's/spouse's name. This change, inspired by a district judge's suggestion, aims to empower women and reflect modern family structures. The move will impact judicial officers' personal files, staff ID cards, and various official forms.

stories.title: Fire at Kolkata warehouse: 7 dead, 21 missing
stories.summary: A devastating fire engulfed a Kolkata warehouse complex early Monday, claiming at least seven lives and leaving 21 workers missing. Trapped inside units laden with combustible decoration materials and food supplies, the victims were sleeping when the blaze erupted. Firefighters battled for hours, but the inferno's intensity and smoldering debris continue to hinder rescue efforts.

stories.title: Alert: UK households urged to stockpile three essentials ahead of Storm Chandra power cut risk
stories.summary: Storm Chandra is set to bring disruptive weather across the UK from late Monday into Tuesday, with heavy rain, strong winds and snow triggering multiple Met Office warnings. Flooding is likely in parts of southern England, while northern England and Scotland face hill snow and travel disruption. Households are urged to prepare for possible power cuts.

stories.title: West Virginia woman arrested in alleged Trump assassination plot; sheriff says she recruit people on social media
stories.summary: A West Virginia woman, Morgan Morrow, faces charges for allegedly attempting to recruit individuals to assassinate President Donald Trump. Authorities apprehended Morrow after discovering a TikTok post where she seemingly solicited a sniper. She reportedly admitted to posting the message, citing personal reasons for her animosity towards the President.

stories.title: ‘Stay away from USA’: Former FIFA chief Sepp Blatter fuels World Cup 2026 boycott debate
stories.summary: Amidst rising geopolitical tensions and concerns over US policies, a growing chorus is calling for a boycott of the 2026 FIFA World Cup co-hosted by the United States. Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter has publicly supported calls for fans to stay away, citing recent incidents and the perceived contradiction with the tournament's spirit of unity.

stories.title: YouTuber WhistlinDiesel faces another tax arrest after previous 2025 case
stories.summary: Popular YouTuber WhistlinDiesel, Cody Detwiler, was arrested again for a $30,000 tax dispute, claiming he received no prior notice. This follows a previous tax evasion arrest in November 2025. Detwiler stated the issue stems from a vehicle registered in Montana that was later destroyed, leading to a prolonged tax case without official notification.

stories.title: 'Maybe Vance wants to signal...': Former Indian diplomat on why JD Vance has been blocking US-India deal
'Attacking H1-B was the best thing...': Canadian-Indian entrepreneur on big tech layoffs in US
MrBeast criticizes Netflix pay, would give Alex Honnold over $500K for Taipei 101 stunt
stories.summary: Daredevil Alex Honnold's breathtaking free solo of Taipei 101 has sparked a bidding war, with YouTuber MrBeast claiming he'd have paid over $500,000 for the stunt on his platform. Honnold's 90-minute climb, broadcast live on Netflix, highlights the growing appeal of extreme urban feats and the fierce competition between streaming giants for high-stakes entertainment.

stories.title: In Republic Day messages, Trump hails historic bond, Xi talks of dragon-elephant tango
stories.summary: Global leaders, including US President Trump and China's Xi Jinping, extended Republic Day greetings to India. Trump emphasized the bond between the world's oldest and largest democracies, while Xi highlighted India-China as "good neighbours, friends and partners." King Charles III also lauded the enduring India-UK partnership, noting shared values and deepening cooperation.

stories.title: 'H-1B is something I have no control of': Indian-origin Frisco councilman Burt Thakur on why he has Indian donors
Bangor plane crash kills 7: Private jet linked to ‘anti‑Trump’ lawyers who defended illegal aliens
Did Tim Walz ask Donald Trump to work together? Minnesota governor, US president have ‘productive’ call over ICE protests
stories.summary: Following the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti by a Border Patrol agent, Minnesota Governor Tim Walz and President Trump held a "productive" call. Trump agreed to allow the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension to investigate the incident and to review reducing federal agent numbers in the state.

stories.title: India, EU finalise FTA, deal set to be announced today
stories.summary: India and the European Union have finalized a comprehensive free trade agreement after 18 years of talks, poised to boost trade and investment. The deal, expected to be announced Tuesday, aims for significant tariff reductions on most goods, with India gaining market access for textiles and leather, while offering concessions on automobiles and wines. Implementation is anticipated by early 2027.

stories.title: Russia to hire 40,000 Indian workers in 2026, paying up to $1,000 amid labour shortage: Report
stories.summary: In a bold move to tackle its acute labor shortage, Russia is gearing up to welcome more than 40,000 Indian workers by 2026. This strategic decision comes in the wake of demographic challenges and an ongoing conflict, underlining the need for skilled labor. Following a recent mobility agreement, many Indian professionals are already contributing to the Russian workforce.

stories.title: Republic Day: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta lays foundation stone for slum development projects
stories.summary: "The previous governments spread fear that the BJP would stop free electricity and water, but these slum dwellers can now live peacefully. We are committed to providing them a good and quality life," Gupta told reporters.

stories.title: PIO civil servant gets flak on X for negotiating Chagos deal
stories.summary: A British civil servant of Indian origin, Dr. Francis Vijay Narasimhan Rangarajan, faces social media backlash over the controversial Chagos deal. He led negotiations to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Archipelago to Mauritius, retaining use of the Diego Garcia base. Critics, including former politicians, have voiced strong opposition to the agreement.

stories.title: 'Boring as hell': Trump reveals why he 'dozes off' during cabinet meeting; has nothing to do with health
'I can handle it': Mark Carney shrugs off Donald Trump’s ‘Governor’ jibe amid 100% tariff threat
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney dismissed Donald Trump's 'Governor' remark, stating he can handle it. Trump, threatening a 100% tariff, accused Canada of becoming a 'Drop Off Port' for Chinese goods. Carney, while not commenting on every tweet, emphasized the importance of respecting Canadian troops amidst the escalating trade tensions.

stories.title: British nationals charged with ‘targeting’ Pakistan dissidents in UK
stories.summary: Three British nationals have been charged with targeting two prominent Pakistani dissidents in the UK, supporters of jailed former PM Imran Khan. The men allegedly conspired to assault journalist Adil Raja and former Khan advisor Mirza Shahzad Akbar on December 24th. One suspect also faces charges for attempted arson at Akbar's home on New Year's Eve.

stories.title: Decline of Himalayan rivers could trigger nuclear war: UK report
stories.summary: UK intelligence warns of global food and water crises by the 2030s due to ecosystem collapse, potentially sparking conflict. Himalayan river decline could escalate tensions between China, India, and Pakistan, risking nuclear war. The report highlights threats to UK food security and calls for ecosystem protection and restoration.

stories.title: A century in uniform: Chandigarh girl carries 4 generations of Army service to Kartavya Path
Kashmir peaceful, ready to welcome visitors: Deputy CM
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary stated that Pakistan's efforts to disrupt tourism in the region have failed. He urged people to visit Kashmir, emphasizing its peaceful atmosphere and readiness to welcome visitors, while also honoring the victims of a past terror attack.

stories.title: From Bathinda to Kartavya Path: Punjab lad commands T-90 Bhishma tank at RD parade
Stage harassment allegation: Former TMC MP Mimi Chakraborty files police complaint
Kashmir braces for heavy snowfall after last week’s spell
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir is preparing for more heavy snowfall. A western disturbance is expected to bring snow starting Monday evening. This could affect flights and the Jammu-Srinagar highway. Moderate to heavy snowfall is forecast for most of Kashmir and higher Jammu regions on Tuesday. Light rain and higher-reach snow are possible Wednesday.

stories.title: ‘Insensitive and insulting’: BJP says Rahul Gandhi declined to wear Assamese Gamosa; Congress counters
stories.summary: The BJP has criticized Rahul Gandhi for allegedly not wearing an Assamese 'Gamosa' at a Republic Day reception, with Assam's CM demanding an apology. Congress countered by questioning why Defence Minister Rajnath Singh wasn't also asked to wear it, accusing the BJP of trivial politics and highlighting alleged disrespect towards their leaders at the parade.

stories.title: Have you ever paid your employer from salary? Immigration expert explains what this question by a border agent to an H-1B worker means
Train to Pahalgam faces backlash; NC, PDP ask railway minister to rethink
stories.summary: A proposed railway line from Bijbehara to Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir is facing strong opposition from local residents and political figures. Concerns are mounting over the project's impact on vast agricultural and apple orchard lands, threatening livelihoods. Leaders are urging the central government to reconsider the plan, citing existing infrastructure and the project's perceived lack of benefit.

stories.title: Could the UK bring back mandatory military service? What happens if you refuse
stories.summary: Amid rising global tensions and a shrinking British Army, the idea of conscription has resurfaced in public debate, though ministers insist there are no plans to reinstate it. Experts suggest modern refusal would likely incur fines rather than imprisonment, with exemptions for essential workers and conscientious objectors. Polls show significant reluctance among younger adults, highlighting challenges if conscription were ever enforced.

stories.title: Iran tensions: US aircraft carrier, warships arrive in Middle East
‘Hindu man looking down...’: Casey Putsch says Vivek Ramaswamy is working with ‘anti-Christ’
Stagger station revamp to prioritise funding of rail corridors, govt panel tells railways
stories.summary: An inter-ministerial panel has advised Indian Railways to stagger station redevelopment projects, prioritizing funding for programmatic corridors. The panel also recommended linking station development expenditure to revenue generation, including user charges, and suggested rolling out Integrated Station Facility Managers to maximize income from station assets.

stories.title: ‘Americans who hate Indians…’: Social media reacts to free samosas given at anti‑ICE protests
Private jet crashes in US: 7 killed, 1 severely injured; aircraft went down shortly after takeoff
‘No anaesthesia for MAGA’: Florida nurse refuses to treat Republicans, sparks calls for suspension
stories.summary: A Florida nurse named Erik Martindale has stirred up a storm on social media after declaring on Facebook that he would deny anesthesia to MAGA supporters. His bold statement has sparked outrage and prompted calls for the revocation of his nursing license. In a twist, Martindale later claimed his social media accounts had been compromised.

stories.title: Russian oil goes to India, Europeans buy refined products from them: Scott Bessent
Mass dog killings rattles Telangana: 200 more canines found dead in Hanamkonda; toll rises to 1,100
Agriculture scientists and innovative farmers get Padma Shri boost for their pioneering efforts
stories.summary: In a grand tribute to innovation in agriculture, nine distinguished individuals have been honored with the Padma Shri. Among them are esteemed scientists and passionate farmers, recognized for their impactful work ranging from the creation of superior rice strains and genome-editing breakthroughs to the promotion of unique cultivation methods such as Makhana farming.

stories.title: ‘No more hostages in Gaza’: IDF recovers last captive held by Hamas; remains repatriated to Israel
stories.summary: The Israeli military has recovered the remains of Ran Gvili, the last hostage held in Gaza, confirming all abductees have been returned to Israel. Prime Minister Netanyahu hailed this as an extraordinary achievement, fulfilling a promise to bring everyone back. Hamas stated the discovery confirms their commitment to the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: ‘Colonial mindset’: Padma Shri row over cow dung, urine remarks; Sridhar Vembu backs IIT Madras director
stories.summary: A political row erupted on social media after the Congress questioned IIT Madras director V Kamakoti's Padma Shri award, linking it to research on cow dung and urine. Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu strongly defended Kamakoti, highlighting his deep tech expertise and the scientific potential of traditional substances, criticizing a "slavish colonial mindset."

stories.title: Tough but fair: Why is Donald Trump sending Tom Homan to Minneapolis in a snub to Kristi Noem?
Who is Suella Braverman? British-Indian leader quits Conservatives and joins Reform UK
J&K: Army soldier injured in landmine blast near LoC in Rajouri
Kristi Noem called ‘sicko fan’ by DHS officials after Minnesota nurse killed by federal agents
Protocol vs politics: Congress questions Rahul's, Kharge's third-row seating at Republic Day parade; BJP hits back
‘Insult to Maharashtra’: Oppn slams Padma Bhushan for Koshiyari; ex-governor shrugs off criticism
stories.summary: Opposition leaders slammed the Centre's decision to award Padma Bhushan to former Maharashtra Governor Bhagat Singh Koshiyari, citing his alleged role in toppling the MVA government and insulting state icons. However, CM Devendra Fadnavis defended the award, highlighting Koshiyari's societal contributions and work for development.

stories.title: 'Self-sabotage': Indian-American entrepreneurs reject JD Vance as 'India's friend' after trade deal 'leaked' audio; 'To appease the groypers'
Mystery solved: What makes the sliding rocks of Death Valley move on their own
After a gap of over 10 years, India marks Republic Day in Yemen
stories.summary: For the first time in over a decade, India celebrated Republic Day in Yemen with the Indian community and embassy staff. Other diplomatic missions in the US, Singapore, Japan, and Sri Lanka also marked the occasion with flag unfurling ceremonies and participation from the Indian diaspora. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio extended greetings, highlighting the strong bilateral partnership.

stories.title: ChatGPT ‘nearly kills’ woman after giving confident advice about a poisonous plant
stories.summary: A YouTuber has warned of the dangers of trusting AI after ChatGPT repeatedly misidentified poison hemlock as harmless carrot foliage, nearly putting her friend at risk. Despite visual evidence, the chatbot doubled down with confident reassurances. The incident highlights how AI errors, especially in health and safety contexts, can have serious real-world consequences.

stories.title: Row over Tulsi Gabbard’s past link to Indian-American lawyer who said ‘kick Trump’
Evening news wrap: India flexes might on 77th Republic Day parade; UAE scraps Pakistan airport deal & more
stories.summary: India marked its 77th Republic Day with a grand parade showcasing military might and cultural diversity. Meanwhile, the UAE reportedly scrapped its airport management deal with Pakistan following the UAE President's India visit. In other news, a Bangladesh court sentenced three police officers to death for protest-related killings, and IndiGo cancelled flights to four Central Asian cities due to regional developments.

stories.title: Canada PM Mark Carney likely to visit India in March: Uranium, trade pact on agenda; comes days after China pivot
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is slated to visit India in early March to sign significant deals on uranium, energy, minerals, AI, education, and culture. This visit aims to diversify Canada's alliances and reset bilateral relations, with formal CEPA negotiations also set to commence. Both nations are prioritizing these agreements amid a changing global order and U.S. trade pressures.

stories.title: MrBeast steps into food tech spotlight after tasting cultivated chicken, drawing millions into future food debate
stories.summary: MrBeast brought cultivated meat into the mainstream after tasting cell-based chicken at Upside Foods’ California facility. His visit offered millions of young followers a rare look at how meat can be grown from cells without slaughter. The moment gave alternative protein a cultural boost, helping shift perception from niche food tech to something familiar and accessible.

stories.title: UAE influencers could face AED 10,000 fine for missing January 31 'Advertiser Permit' deadline
stories.summary: UAE content creators and advertisers must secure a mandatory Advertiser Permit by January 31, 2026, to avoid fines up to AED 10,000. This new regulation by the UAE Media Council aims to enhance transparency and professionalism in the digital advertising landscape.

stories.title: 'Dragon and elephant dance together': China's Xi greets President Droupadi Murmu on 77th Republic Day
“The only race of women who….”: Social media erupts as Clavicular’s comments about Black women trigger backlash
stories.summary: Clavicular is facing backlash after a viral clip showed him bluntly dismissing interest in Black women. The resurfaced comment sparked intense fan reaction, with social media users debating dating culture, racial fixation, and why such remarks continue to dominate online conversations. The clip quickly crossed millions of views, amplifying criticism and discourse.

stories.title: January 26, 1950: Revisiting India’s first Republic Day — the parade and those who watched history unfold
stories.summary: India celebrated its 77th Republic Day with a grand parade on Kartavya Path, showcasing military might and cultural diversity. The event marked the EU's first military parade participation outside Europe, reflecting India's growing global ties. The celebrations honored the nation's journey since becoming a sovereign democratic republic on January 26, 1950.

stories.title: One vote, unequal weight: Kothnur has just 10.9k elections, RR Nagar nearly 50k
stories.summary: Bengaluru's new municipal structure reveals significant voter disparities across wards, with some representing over 49,000 electors while others have just over 10,000. This imbalance undermines democratic representation and could lead to unequal access to civic services and political influence. The delimitation process, based on 2011 census population figures, has resulted in these inequities.

stories.title: Who is the owner of Greenland: Inside the story of the Viking murderer who named the land and built a lost Norse world
77th R-Day: Donald Trump extends greetings on Republic Day; hails India-US ties as a ‘historic bond’ of world’s largest democracies
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump extended heartfelt greetings to India on its 77th Republic Day, highlighting the "historic partnership" between the world's oldest and largest democracies. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Ambassador Sergio Gor also conveyed wishes, emphasizing strong cooperation across various sectors and the symbolic presence of US-made aircraft at the parade.

stories.title: Bangladesh crisis: Tribunal sentences 3 police officers to death; 5 others get jail terms
‘We all benefit’: EU chief says ‘successful India makes world more stable’, after attending Republic Day parade
stories.summary: European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen stated that a successful India contributes to global stability, prosperity, and security. She, along with European Council president Antonio Costa, were the first joint EU leaders to attend India's Republic Day parade as chief guests. Their visit precedes an India-EU summit focused on trade, security, and strategic cooperation.

stories.title: THIS world’s largest underground city under Cappadocia kept 20,000 people alive without seeing daylight
Ramadan 2026: Expected dates, fasting hours, and seasonal shifts explained
stories.summary: Muslims worldwide anticipate a more moderate Ramadan in 2026, with fasting hours expected between 12-13 hours in Arab nations. This shift from recent summer fasts, due to the holy month falling in late winter/early spring, promises cooler temperatures and shorter daylight. Even in higher latitudes, fasting will be less demanding than previous years.

stories.title: Army’s 'phased battle array', IAF flypast and cultural diversity take centre stage — key takeaways from 77th Republic Day
stories.summary: India celebrates its 77th Republic Day on Monday, with nationwide events marking the adoption of the Constitution and highlighting the country’s cultural and military heritage. Celebrations of the 77th Republic Day at the Kartvya Path were based on the theme of the 150th Anniversary of the national song, Vande Mataram, a timeless mantra that awakened the spirit of Swadeshi, self-reliance, and freedom in India's national consciousness.

stories.title: Frozen America: A brutal winter storm has gripped the United States - in pics
stories.summary: A massive winter storm battered large parts of the United States, bringing heavy snow, sleet and freezing rain that disrupted travel, power supply and daily life. Millions were placed under winter weather warnings as Arctic cold followed the system, pushing temperatures to dangerous lows. Flight cancellations surged across major airports, while power outages left homes and businesses in the dark, especially in southern states unaccustomed to severe ice. Cities from New York and Washington to Chicago and Philadelphia struggled with icy roads and emergency closures. Authorities warned that extreme cold could prolong disruptions and pose life-threatening risks.

stories.title: This 3,000-year-old treasure in Spain was made with iron that fell from the sky
BrahMos to S-400: Weapon systems from Operation Sindoor take centre stage at Republic Day parade
stories.summary: India's Republic Day 2026 parade showcased its military might, highlighting the success of Operation Sindoor, a counterterror action that neutralized over 100 terrorists and enemy soldiers. The display featured advanced weapons platforms like the BrahMos missile and S-400 air defence system, emphasizing combat readiness and technological prowess in multi-domain warfare.

stories.title: World’s longest road tunnel takes drivers on a 20-minute journey without daylight beneath Norway’s mountains
Dubai’s Gulfood 2026: Two venues, 8,500 exhibitors and the world’s biggest food show
stories.summary: Gulfood 2026, the world's largest food trade show, has doubled its exhibition space across two Dubai venues for the first time in its 31-year history. This expansion accommodates over 8,500 exhibitors from 195 countries, showcasing 1.5 million products. The move aims to solidify Dubai's position as the global food trade headquarters, offering a more organized and expansive sourcing experience.

stories.title: Qatar Labour Ministry urges worker safety amid dusty, windy conditions in Doha
stories.summary: Doha faces dusty and windy weather. The Ministry of Labour has issued an advisory to employers. Companies must step up safety measures for outdoor workers. Protective equipment and adjusted schedules are crucial. This ensures worker wellbeing and safe work environments amidst adverse conditions. Continuous monitoring of weather is advised.

stories.title: 77th Republic Day: PM Modi dons maroon-yellow Rajasthani safa with zari motifs
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's red Rajasthani turban, adorned with golden-yellow streaks, captivated onlookers at the 77th Republic Day parade. This distinctive headwear, a recurring signature, symbolizes India's rich cultural tapestry and regional heritage. Paired with a navy kurta-pyjama and light blue Nehru jacket, his attire blended formal elegance with cultural pride, complementing the grandeur of the national celebration.

stories.title: Vikings reached America 1,000 years before Christopher Columbus; scientists confirm
